catalogTitle: “ולאדם לא מצא עזר כנגדו” - זה קוב"ה וכנסת ישראל

oneLiner.en: Starting from the Mishnah's sign of rain in the sukkah, the Mashgiach explains that the yearly path from Rosh Hashanah to Shemini Atzeres repeats the creation of Chava, the bond of Hashem and Knesses Yisrael, and that a broken Sukkos can be rebuilt from Bereishis.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Mishnah in Sukkah that rain driving one out of the sukkah is like a servant whose master throws the cup back in his face, and asks why the Rambam limits this sign to the start of the festival. He explains that only the first night carries an obligation, and that the mitzvah of sukkah is dwelling: like a home address, it stays even when rain sends a person out, while the kezayis on the first night is what fixes the sukkah as his home for all seven days. He then turns to the parsha: the creation of Chava for Adam repeats every year between Hashem and Knesses Yisrael, from Rosh Hashanah through Yom Kippur and Sukkos to the union of Shemini Atzeres. He contrasts erusin and nisuin, explains rain on Sukkos as the Satan's share at a time of great holiness, and closes that broken luchos lead back to Bereishis, where one can begin again.

en: According to the Mashgiach, rain is a bad sign only on the first night of Sukkos, because only then is there an obligation to eat in the sukkah; on other days a person has a choice.
The mitzvah of sukkah is to dwell there; like an address, the sukkah stays one's home even when rain sends him out.
The kezayis eaten on the first night establishes the sukkah as one's dwelling for all seven days, a stronger fixing than the meal placed for an eruv.
The creation of Chava and her coming to Adam repeats every year between Hashem and Knesses Yisrael, from Rosh Hashanah to Shemini Atzeres.
Nisuin is a closer bond than erusin, yet its punishment is lighter, because it comes from the attribute of chesed.
The rain on Sukkos is the Satan's share at a time of great holiness, and a sign that a year of union with Hashem is approaching.
The breaking of the luchos is joined to Bereishis: after a broken Sukkos one can begin again.

title.en: Rain in the sukkah: the Rambam's limit

summary.en: The Mashgiach learns the Mishnah in Sukkah about leaving the sukkah in rain and its parable of the servant whose cup is thrown back at him. He brings the Rambam's commentary that the bad sign applies only at the start of the festival, and explains that only the first night is an obligation, so rain then cancels a mitzvah one had no choice about.

title.en: The sukkah as one's address

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why one who suffers is exempt from the sukkah, and why one must eat a kezayis there on the first night like matzah. He explains that the mitzvah is to dwell in the sukkah: like a person whose address stays on his street even when he is elsewhere, one who leaves for rain still lives in his sukkah.

title.en: The first night fixes the dwelling

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the first-night kezayis is what establishes the sukkah as one's home for seven days, comparing it to the meal that fixes a person's place for an eruv, though sukkah needs a stronger fixing. If it rains that night the dwelling was never established, which is why the Mishnah stresses 'all seven days' and why the sign applies then.

title.en: Chava's creation, renewed every Tishrei

summary.en: Turning to the parsha, the Mashgiach brings that the process from 'for Adam no helpmate was found' until Chava is brought to Adam happens every year with every Jew: Knesses Yisrael is the woman and Hashem the man. He traces it through Rosh Hashanah and the shofar, the separation of Yom Kippur, the sukkah as a chuppah and Shemini Atzeres as the climax, and returns to the Mishnah's servant: on Rosh Hashanah the Jews stood as servants.

title.en: Erusin and nisuin

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Adam slept and was passive while Chava was built. He then asks why an arusah who sins is punished with stoning while a nesuah, more closely bound to her husband, receives the lighter death of strangling, and answers with the Ramban that what comes from love is lighter in punishment, as Yom Kippur is lighter than Shabbos; nisuin raises the wife to become one with her husband.

title.en: Souls already joined; lost item and find

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a match is not made from outside: the souls of a man and his wife were bound together from the start, and Adam's rib showed this once for all later generations. He distinguishes, regarding shidduchim, between seeking a lost item and seeking a find, contrasting one who demands qualifications with one who accepts what is given.

title.en: Adam and Chava began with nisuin

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Bereishis contains everything, and that the parsha ends with the 'sons of the powerful' taking wives, a decline that led to the world's destruction. He explains that the letter heh marks the completeness of a woman, attained at nisuin, and that Adam and Chava began at once with nisuin: 'this time' only, for later history would begin with erusin.

title.en: Knesses Yisrael's Tishrei, and the Satan's bone

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies the parsha to Klal Yisrael, sanctified to Hashem as 'Yisrael is holy to Hashem', rising through Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Sukkos to the union of Shemini Atzeres, after the seventy nations, like wedding guests, have gone home. With a parable of a dog at a laden table he explains that at a time of great holiness the Satan demands a share, and so the rain came on Sukkos.

title.en: Servant and son; holiness kept hidden

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a Jew serves as a servant through the deeds of the mitzvos and as a son through his heart, so being driven from the sukkah pains the servant within while the heart is still bound. He then says that what is done in public draws harm, as the first luchos were broken, and that matters of kedushah must be kept hidden so the Satan does not interfere.

title.en: Moshiach comes concealed: Peretz and Zerach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the soul of Moshiach comes in concealment, as with Yehudah and Tamar, and that the main union of Knesses Yisrael is at the kedushah of Simchas Torah. He brings the birth of Peretz and Zerach and Rashi's teaching that Achan descended from Zerach, describing how the Satan sought to block Moshiach's line.

title.en: This year's rain; from broken luchos to Bereishis

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the unprecedented rain of this Sukkos as an accusation that prepares the salvation of Shemini Atzeres, brings the Gemara in Avodah Zarah on the nations kicking the sukkah, and asks his listeners to hold firm to emunah in Moshiach's coming. He links the breaking of the luchos at the Torah's end to Bereishis, which contains everything, so that after a broken Sukkos one can start again.

title.en: Words to the yeshiva

summary.en: The Mashgiach addresses the yeshiva: with a saying contrasting sugar and rock candy he explains that a chassid sweetens others, and he asks older bochurim to give time to help the younger ones. He mentions learning Kiddushin this year and closes with a wish for union with Hashem in Yerushalayim.

catalogTitle: The Special Holiness of נח תיבת: a Microcosm of the עולם התיקון

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Noach's Teivah was a holy island of the perfected world, where even the lion ate grass, until Cham's sin brought back the curse, and that Hashem still remembered Noach with love because Avraham and the Jewish people would come from him.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the contrast between Noach finding favor, an unearned gift, and being called a tzaddik. Cheshvan's combination of Hashem's Name, drawn from 'u'dvash' ending one passuk in Devarim into the next, teaches that the honey of Tishrei must be carried into Cheshvan, the month of decay. In Zichronos we recall that Hashem remembered Noach with love, and the Mashgiach asks why love was needed when the rescue was planned, and why the lion could wound Noach. He explains that man's deeds govern creation: the generation's sin corrupted even the animals and the soil, while Noach's portion stayed pure. The Teivah was a sanctuary like the world before Adam's sin, where the lion needed no meat. Cham's sin spoiled it, the lion needed meat, and Noach was wounded. Hashem still remembered him for the sake of Avraham, which gives encouragement in Cheshvan.

en: Cheshvan, the month of Bul, of withering and decay, follows Tishrei, and the Mashgiach says the sweetness and renewal of Tishrei must be carried into it.
In the Zichronos of Rosh Hashanah we recall that Hashem remembered Noach with love, and the Mashgiach asks why that love was needed when the whole rescue had been planned in advance.
Man stands at the control center of creation: the sins of the generation of the Mabul were mirrored in the animals and even in the soil, while the part of creation under Noach stayed pure.
The Teivah was a place of kedushah like the world before Adam's sin, and there the lion did not need meat.
Cham's sin in the Teivah brought back the curse, the lion needed meat and wounded Noach, yet Hashem remembered Noach with love because Avraham and the Jewish people would come from him.

the sin of Cham in the Teivah

title.en: Favor or righteousness; Cheshvan after Tishrei

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts 'Noach found favor', which the Midrash reads as an unearned gift, with the next passuk calling Noach a tzaddik. He then notes that Cheshvan has begun and that people still long for the honey-sweet days and prayers of Tishrei.

title.en: Cheshvan's combination of Hashem's Name

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that each month is governed by one of the twelve combinations of Hashem's Name, each derived from a passuk. Cheshvan's combination, vav-hei-hei-yud, comes from 'u'dvash' at the end of one passuk in Devarim and the opening words of the next, the only combination that runs from one passuk into another.

title.en: Bringing Tishrei's honey into the month of Bul

summary.en: Tishrei is a month of honey, and 'Av HaRachaman' has the gematria of 'dvash', 306. Cheshvan, called Bul in Tanach, is the month of decay, so the combination runs from 'u'dvash' into 'hayom hazeh': with Rashi's 'every day they should be new in your eyes', the Mashgiach says the renewal of Tishrei must be carried into Cheshvan.

title.en: Zichronos: why Noach needed to be remembered

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the Zichronos blessing of Rosh Hashanah, whose first passuk tells how Hashem remembered Noach and passed a wind over the earth so the waters receded. He asks why Hashem had to remember Noach with love when the whole plan of the Teivah had been told to Noach 120 years earlier.

title.en: The lion that wounded Noach

summary.en: The Mabul wiped out every trace of the old world. Rashi on 'ach Noach' says Noach was late in feeding the lion, which wounded him. The Mashgiach brings the Ramban that the Teivah was a great miracle, small yet holding every species, and asks: if Hashem helped Noach with everything, why was the lion allowed to injure him?

title.en: Could Noach have brought meat?

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ibn Ezra, who answers those who ask where Noach found meat that the lion could eat straw, and argues from Chazal that Noach brought each creature its own food. Since Rashi says Hashem promised that the food would not rot, Noach could have brought meat, so why did he fail to feed the lion?

title.en: When Moshiach comes: the lion will eat straw

summary.en: Recalling a song mothers sang about what will be when Moshiach comes, the Mashgiach says that era already existed before Adam's sin, when lions and tigers ate grass. He brings Yeshayahu's prophecy of the wolf with the sheep and the lion eating straw, and the Ramban that wild beasts were meant to be gentle and became predators only through Adam's sin.

title.en: Man's deeds rule creation; Noach's portion

summary.en: Man was made to rule creation, and through mitzvos and aveiros he perfects or spoils it. Rashi says even the animals of the Mabul's generation were corrupt, which the Mashgiach explains as man's sin mirrored in them, and even the topsoil was wiped away. Noach's portion, the animals that came to the Teivah and Eretz Yisrael, where no Mabul fell, stayed pure.

title.en: The Teivah as a sanctuary and a utopia

summary.en: Hashem created a perfect world in Adam's time; Adam's sin spoiled it until, ten generations later, even animals and soil were corrupt. Noach, his family and his animals were to be the embryo of a new world. The Mashgiach explains that the Teivah, built to exact dimensions like the Mishkan and the Beis HaMikdash, was a place of kedushah, heaven on earth, exempt from the Mabul, a society of tzaddikim like the world before the sin.

title.en: Why the lion eats meat; Cham's sin

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that life in food is Hashem's word; a tzaddik extracts it from little, a kosher animal draws it from grass, but the cruel, unclean lion cannot and needs concentrated food, meat. In the Teivah's utopia the lion did not need meat and Noach brought none. Then, as Rashi explains, Cham, the raven and the dog violated the prohibition on cohabitation in the Teivah and were cursed.

title.en: Digression on the curse of Cham

summary.en: In a digression the Mashgiach contrasts the Torah's account of Noach cursing Cham with the outlook of a society that does not live by the Torah, insisting this does not mean Torah Jews look down on other people, since all men are created equal, while holding that the curse remains until its cause is removed in the days of Moshiach.

title.en: The utopia lost, and Hashem's love for Noach

summary.en: Cham's sin spoiled the Teivah as Adam's sin spoiled Eden; Noach left it no longer holy and planted a vineyard, repeating the sin of the Eitz HaDaas. Now the lion needed meat, Noach had none, and the lion wounded him, and Hashem did not help. Hashem could have left them stranded, but remembered Noach with love because Avraham and the Jewish people, who will bring the world to its perfection, would come from him.

title.en: Encouragement for Cheshvan: the third world

summary.en: In Zichronos we ask Hashem to spare us as He spared Noach, for the sake of what will come. The Mashgiach explains that Hashem makes three tries: two worlds, Adam's and Noach's, were spoiled, and the third will be perfect, like the third Beis HaMikdash. The Mabul began in Cheshvan, and in Cheshvan, disappointed with Tishrei, we take encouragement from the sedra, which ends with the birth of Avraham Avinu.

catalogTitle: “מה טעם פתח בבראשית!” ווי געשמאק אז מען פאנגט אן פון בראשית!

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why it is so sweet to begin again from Bereishis: the word Bereishis contains the whole Torah, emunah, Shabbos, Moshe Rabbeinu and Moshiach, and Shabbos Bereishis is a last chance to set the whole year right by asking Hashem for an undeserved gift.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Rimanover's exclamation on why the Torah begins with Bereishis: how sweet it is. Bereishis contains the whole Torah, from its first letter to the end of the parsha. He praises the simple emunah of Yidden in their minhagim, explaining that emunah comes from the height of the mind, not its weakness, and that Bereishis, above the ten utterances, is the root of emunah. Bereishis also hints at fear of Heaven and at Shabbos, the purpose of creation. Since the Torah stands above time, Shabbos Bereishis is the place to appeal what was decided in Tishrei. He then describes how to keep Shabbos with holiness, how Moshe Rabbeinu blows Shabbos into every heart, and how Noach found favor by asking for an undeserved gift. Finally he shows that Bereishis hints at Moshiach, who will come with open miracles, and urges a Shabbos Bereishis of great preparation.

en: The word Bereishis, and the first parsha up to 'v'Noach matza chen', contains the whole Torah.
The emunah of Yidden, even in local minhagim, comes from the height of the intellect, things above the mind, and not from its weakness.
Since the Torah, which created time, is above time, the parsha of Bereishis is the place to appeal what was decreed for the year.
Shabbos is a day of the soul; its physical pleasures are meant to be raised into holiness and the service of Hashem.
One who feels he deserves nothing can ask for a matnas chinam, an undeserved gift, from the greatest of Hashem's treasuries, as Noach did.
Bereishis hints at Moshiach, and the end of the Torah, with its open miracles, is joined to its beginning to show that the redemption will come with miracles like those of Yetzias Mitzrayim.

candidateTopics: Shabbos as a day of the soul

title.en: How sweet to begin with Bereishis; emunah in minhagim

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Rimanover's words on why the Torah begins with Bereishis and explains that Bereishis contains the whole Torah. He then praises the emunah of Yidden in their minhagim and explains that true emunah comes from the height of the intellect, so that 'the testimony of Hashem makes the simple wise'.

title.en: Bereishis, the root of emunah; the value of small minhagim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Bereishis stands above the other utterances of creation, before words and letters, and is the root of all emunah. He discusses the minhag of round challos and tells how the Chasam Sofer measured Moses Mendelssohn by whether he still kept the Shavuos minhag of greenery, concluding that Yiddishkeit is measured by small things.

title.en: Bereishis contains creation, fear of Heaven and Shabbos

summary.en: Citing the Pri Tzaddik and the Tikkunei Zohar, the Mashgiach shows that the word Bereishis contains all of creation and reads as 'yarei shamayim', 'bris esh' and 'yarei Shabbos'. He explains with a mashal of a man who builds and furnishes a house in order to learn that Shabbos, the purpose of creation, was first in thought and is hinted in Bereishis.

title.en: Shabbos Bereishis as the court of appeal

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Baal HaTanya in the name of the Ba'al Shem Tov that on Shabbos Bereishis a person's whole year is determined. He explains that time was created from the Torah, which stands above time, so whoever feels he did not use the days of Tishrei can go to the 'supreme court', the parsha of Bereishis, and appeal.

title.en: Haazinu and Bereishis; the Shabbos of all Shabbosos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Haazinu contains the whole Torah as its end and Bereishis as its beginning, and that the Torah ends with 'Yisrael' and begins with 'Bereishis', linking the letters of the Torah to the souls of Yisrael. Shabbos Bereishis contains all Shabbosos and stands above the utterances decreed on Rosh Hashanah; he tells of the Lechovitcher's words about Rabbi Mendel of Vitebsk's love of Shabbos.

title.en: Shabbos as a day of the soul

summary.en: The Mashgiach says one must learn the halachos of Shabbos and go further, feeling holiness on Shabbos, which is not a weekend but a day of the soul. With a mashal of a prince who won back his father by turning his low companions into loyal servants, he explains that oneg Shabbos means bringing physical things into holiness, and that menuchah is the contentment that comes from that holiness.

title.en: Moshe Rabbeinu blows Shabbos into every heart

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar that Moshe Rabbeinu comes each Shabbos with a thousand souls to blow Shabbos into every Jewish heart, and shows that Bereishis hints at Moshe, who was given the task of making Shabbos known. He describes how Yidden once spoke only words of holiness on Shabbos, and tells how the Lechovitcher gave Rabbi Michel a glass of mead every erev Shabbos to give him strength for his fiery Shabbos.

title.en: Asking for a matnas chinam, like Noach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Moshe Rabbeinu was shown the treasuries in Heaven, the greatest of which was the treasury of matnas chinam, given only to one who feels he deserves nothing. He reads 'v'Noach matza chen' as Noach, who also deserved to be erased, asking for an undeserved gift, and says that on Shabbos Bereishis one should ask the same.

title.en: Avner hinted in the middle letters; Noach's true chen

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the story of the Ramban and his student Avner, hinted in the third letters of a passuk in Haazinu, and asks why the middle letters, explaining that the erasure of a Jew can only be temporary. He then explains that the first parsha cannot end with erasure and so ends with 'v'Noach matza chen', and brings the Divrei Shmuel that the generation of the flood found charm in physical things while Noach found chen in holiness.

title.en: Moshiach in Bereishis and the miracles of the redemption

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Chazal that 'the spirit of Elokim' in Bereishis is the spirit of Moshiach, and links the end of the Torah, with its open miracles, to its beginning. Through the Gemara in Berachos on 'ad ya'avor', he explains that sin can hold back promised miracles, but a promise made with the Name Havaya must be fulfilled, so the final redemption will come with miracles like Yetzias Mitzrayim and one should not be misled into calling natural events the redemption.

title.en: Joining the Torah's end to its beginning

summary.en: The Mashgiach cites the minhag of beginning Bereishis right after finishing the Torah so as not to give the Satan an opening, and offers his own reading of the juxtaposition based on the Yismach Moshe: Bereishis hints at Moshiach and at Moshe Rabbeinu, and the end of the Torah tells of the great miracles done with the Name of Hashem, so Moshiach too will come with open wonders. He returns to the Gemara on why there were no miracles in Ezra's time.

title.en: A personal redemption on Shabbos Bereishis

summary.en: The Mashgiach adds a second difference between the two passages, 'amcha' versus 'am zu', and concludes that Yidden must wait for the real redemption with miracles in this time of hester panim. Bereishis holds a personal redemption for every Jew, and he urges taking this Shabbos with great preparation as the last chance, asking that Yidden find favor in Hashem's eyes like Noach and for a good Bereishis for all of Klal Yisrael.

catalogTitle: לימוד משידוך הראשון - שנעשה בלי השתתפות של מעשי אדם

oneLiner.en: From the first shidduch in the Torah, which came to Adam only when he stopped searching and slept, the Mashgiach teaches bitachon, and then explains Rashi's question why the Torah opens with Bereishis through three 'Torahs': of creation, of man and of Yisrael.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the principle that the first appearance of a thing in the Torah, the blueprint of the world, defines it. The first 'ezer' is the woman: Adam went through all the animals and found no partner, and only when Hashem cast sleep on him did he receive her. Help comes from Hashem, not from running around. He develops this with Chizkiyahu, who slept while Sancheriv's camp fell, with Yaakov, the father of bitachon, with the sukkah, whose essence is sleeping, and with the levels in gathering the manna. He then turns to Rashi's question why the Torah begins with Bereishis. The Torah holds three Torahs: of creation, which nature keeps without choice; of man, the seven mitzvos of Noach; and of Yisrael. Mankind failed three times, control passed to Avraham, and Eretz Yisrael, the center of creation, is claimed by all. All of Bereishis is the introduction to 'Hachodesh hazeh lachem'.

en: Adam found his ezer only after his own search through all the animals failed and Hashem cast sleep on him: real help comes from Hashem, not from one's own running.
The sukkah is the shelter of bitachon, the mark of Yaakov Avinu, the father of bitachon, and from Sukkos one takes bitachon for the whole year.
The Mashgiach raises Rashi's question why the Torah does not begin with the first mitzvah, and Rashi's answer that the nations should not be able to call the Jews robbers.
The Torah contains three Torahs: the Torah of creation, the Torah of man given to the nations, and the Torah of Yisrael.
Creation was put under the control of man; when man keeps his Torah, nature keeps its Torah, and after three failures Hashem gave the keys to Avraham and his children.
Eretz Yisrael is the center and foundation of creation, which is why all the nations want a share in it.
All of Bereishis is an introduction to 'Hachodesh hazeh lachem', explaining why the Torah of Yisrael was given only to the Jews.

title.en: The first ezer: Adam's search for a partner

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that the first samech in the Torah is at the creation of the woman, and explains that the Torah is the blueprint of the world, so the first 'ezer' in it teaches what help is. Adam went through all the animals and found no partner; only when Hashem cast sleep on him and took his rib did he open his eyes and recognize his ezer.

title.en: Help comes from Hashem: sleep, Yaakov and the sukkah

summary.en: The Mashgiach draws the lesson that a person cannot get his ezer by running around; it comes from Hashem. He brings the Midrash on the kings, where Chizkiyahu said he would sleep and Hashem would fight, as happened with Sancheriv's camp, and the Midrash on Yaakov, the father of bitachon, who had nothing yet did not lose his trust. The sukkah, a flimsy hut open to rain, is the shelter of bitachon, and the Gemara speaks of sleeping in it because only one who feels secure can sleep.

title.en: Levels of bitachon: the manna and the lesson of bitul

summary.en: The Mashgiach cites the Chovos Halevavos in Shaar HaBitachon against the belief that one must chase extra jobs all day, and brings the levels at which the Jews gathered the manna: some ran out early, others went farther, and the tzaddikim who davened and learned found it at their door. He concludes that the first ezer in the Torah came after all Adam's efforts failed, and teaches bitul.

title.en: Rashi's question and the three Torahs

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi's question why the Torah did not begin with the first mitzvah given to Yisrael, and the answer that the nations should not call the Jews robbers, and asks why the nations still cry 'robbers' today. He sets out the order of the Torah: it contains three Torahs, of creation, of man and of Yisrael, and the Torah of creation runs from the first passuk of Bereishis.

title.en: Nature is a Torah, and a miracle changes it

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Shabbos about the man for whom a miracle happened to nurse his child, and its criticism that the order of creation was changed for him. He explains that all of nature is written in the pesukim of Bereishis, as whole masechtos rest on a few words, so a bird flying or a tree giving fruit fulfills the Torah like a Jew putting on tefillin, only without choice. A miracle therefore changes the Torah, and tzaddikim held back from making miracles.

title.en: The Torah of man: creation in man's hands

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the Torah of man: Hashem put all of nature under man, and the Gemara in Sanhedrin derives the seven mitzvos of Noach from one passuk. When man keeps his Torah, creation keeps its Torah; in the generation of the flood even the animals stopped keeping theirs, while in the generation of the desert all of nature flourished, and after the churban it declined. Because mankind sinned, Hashem took the control from them and after the generation of the dispersion gave it to Avraham Avinu.

title.en: Three strikes, and the last chance at Sinai

summary.en: The Mashgiach lays out the order of Bereishis as three strikes: Adam's sin with the Tree of Knowledge, the flood and the generation of the dispersion, after which the keys of creation passed to Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov and the shevatim. At the giving of the Torah Hashem gave the nations a last chance, going to Esav and Yishmael, who refused. All these stories are an introduction to 'Hachodesh hazeh lachem', the Torah of Yisrael given only to the Jews.

title.en: Why the nations claim Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how the nations can claim the land from the Jews, when every land in history, America included, was taken by conquest, and conquest is a kinyan, as the Rambam explains about the kedushah of the land. He answers that Eretz Yisrael is different: it is the center of creation, where the world was founded and the Beis Hamikdash is hinted in the word Bereishis, so everyone wants a share. From Hevel through the Crusades to the daily newspapers, the wars center on it, and the seven nations include all seventy.

title.en: All of Bereishis as an introduction to Hachodesh

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Torah did not open with 'Hachodesh hazeh lachem', since the most important comes first, and answers that the nations would ask why only the Jews received the Torah of Yisrael. Bereishis is a chapter of history: the nations had their chances, failed at the flood and the dispersion, and Hashem chose Avraham, swore the land to the Avos, and only then gave the Torah of Yisrael. The nations do not admit it now, but when Moshiach comes they will see the reason.

catalogTitle: הגנת התיבה כמו הגנת הסוכה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the teiva protected Noach the way the sukkah protects a Jew, through its halachos rather than its wood, and that every Jew must now build a teiva of luminous words of Torah and tefillah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Gemara that at Matan Torah the nations feared a new flood, and with the Gemara that Moshe's root lies in the flood generation: Moshe was Noach returned to repair his failure to daven for his generation. Rain's inner content is Torah; Noach's generation, sunk in physicality, received only the outer shell, a destroying flood, while at Sinai the same downpour came as Torah, threefold and lasting. From Shemini Atzeres and the arba minim he moves to the sukkah: its protection comes from its halachos, like a mikveh, and it is an embassy of heaven where judgment cannot reach. So too Noach was saved by the halachos of the teiva, and learning Parshas Noach continues the sukkah's protection. He applies this to the war that broke out on Yom Kippur, the prophecy of Gog and Magog, and Moshe's teiva, and ends with the Ba'al Shem Tov's 'make light in the teiva': every Jew must build a teiva of Torah and tefillah big enough for all Jews.

en: The inner content of rain is Torah; the flood was the outer shell of the very influx that was meant to bring the Torah in Noach's time.
The sukkah protects not through its schach but through its halachos, just as a mikveh purifies through its halachos and not through the water.
Noach was saved by the halachos of the teiva, not by the wooden box itself; the teiva was a sukkah.
Learning Parshas Noach after Sukkos continues the sukkah's protection over the Jewish people.
Every word of Torah and tefillah is a teiva that rescues a Jew from the flood of this world, and it must be said with light and vitality.
Every Jew must build a teiva for all of Klal Yisroel, because every Jew is precious to Hashem.

title.en: A flood at Matan Torah; Moshe as Noach

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Gemara that the nations, hearing the tumult of Matan Torah, asked Bilam whether a flood was coming. He then brings the Gemara that Moshe is hinted in 'b'shagam' of the flood, and explains that Moshe was Noach returned to repair his failure to daven for his generation.

title.en: Rain's inner content is Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that rain carries an inner content, Torah, bringing the Chasam Sofer's reading of the Shema and the link of Shemini Atzeres to Simchas Torah. Noach's generation, sunk in physicality, received only the outer shell, a flood; at Sinai rain came with Torah, and Bilam told the nations it was a 'potion of life', not destruction.

title.en: Forty days, open heavens, threefold Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach draws parallels between the flood and Matan Torah: forty days each and the heavens opened. He brings the Gemara that the Torah is threefold and the Maharal that whatever endures is threefold, shows it in the shin of the tefillin, and explains that Bilam's 'shalom' meant an influx of permanence.

title.en: Arba minim as weapons, sukkah as defense

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the longing when Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah pass. He brings the Midrash that the arba minim are weapons that drive away the forces of evil, while the sukkah is the defense, and describes how, in Rabbi Akiva's view, the Jews sat in real sukkos during the war against Og and were protected.

title.en: The halachos of the sukkah protect

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks where the protection of a flimsy sukkah lies and answers that it is the halachos of the sukkah, which bring down supernal lights, just as the halachos of a mikveh, not its water, purify. He shows it with Yaakov, who after fleeing Esav made sukkos for protection.

title.en: Sukkah as heaven's embassy; the teiva's halachos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the sukkah is like an embassy of heaven on earth, where judgment cannot reach. So Noach, who also deserved judgment, was told to build a teiva with exact halachos, like the Mishkan, sukkah and mikveh; the halachos of the teiva, not the wood, saved him.

title.en: Parshas Noach continues the sukkah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the sweetness of sitting in the sukkah and the longing when it ends, and explains that Hashem gives an extra gift, Parshas Noach: learning about the teiva and its halachos draws the same protection onto the world.

title.en: A war in a season of protection

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the present hard time, when much Jewish blood was spilled, and says that Hashem placed it in a season of protection: Yom Kippur, Sukkos and Parshas Noach. He says the fallen who were killed for being Jews are not to be pitied, but their widows and orphans are, and that no one knows how great the chevlei Moshiach had to be.

title.en: No one knows the end; Rav Elchonon on the state

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the poskim that the war of Gog and Magog will be in Tishrei, and stresses that no one knows the end: even Yaakov, Daniel and the prophets did not. He brings the Rambam on Rabbi Akiva and Bar Koziva and Rav Elchonon Wasserman's statement that redemption cannot come through those who lead the people away from Torah, and says the political state is perhaps a test, while the finest part of Torah today is in Eretz Yisroel.

title.en: Yechezkel's prophecy of Gog and Magog

summary.en: The Mashgiach learns through Yechezkel's prophecy read on Sukkos, explaining 'Rosh' and 'Meshech' as Russia and Moscow and citing a tradition from the Vilna Gaon that Gog and Magog is Russia. He says the prophecy is like a mitzvah that history must fulfill, brings the Gemara on Chizkiyahu and Sanheriv, and reads the pesukim with Rashi on the land gathered from many nations.

title.en: Kiddush Hashem and the Sukkos disappointment

summary.en: The Mashgiach finishes the prophecy's end, a great kiddush Hashem, and says that after the chillul Hashem when the war broke out on Yom Kippur, the teshuvah must be a kiddush Hashem. He stresses that pesukim are understood only when they happen, bringing Rashi and the Ramban on 'v'noshantem', and speaks of the disappointment of those who hoped for salvation this Sukkos.

title.en: Moshe in the teiva: failure that was salvation

summary.en: The Mashgiach retells how Miriam prophesied the redeemer's birth, how Moshe was hidden three months and then placed in a teiva on the day that later became Shavuos, and how Miriam was asked where her prophecy was. Through the Maharal he shows that this apparent failure was the start of the redemption, and suggests that this Sukkos may also prove to have been a salvation.

title.en: Why the mazalos stopped during the flood

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that the mazalos did not function during the flood and asks why. He answers that a decree of destruction for a set time could be interrupted by bright days whose mazal brings kindness, so the mazalos had to stop; Hashem's kindness now was to place the din in the luminous days of Yom Kippur, Sukkos and Parshas Noach.

title.en: 'Make light in the teiva': words of Torah and tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ba'al Shem Tov that teiva means 'word': every word of Torah and tefillah must shine with vitality, and it is the teiva that saves a Jew from the flood of heresy and the yetzer hara of this world. A person who davens without his heart is thrown out of the teiva; with the present danger, he asks who will build the teiva if not the Jews who still learn and say Tehillim.

title.en: Every Jew must be a Noach

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the Torah is eternal: if there was once a Noach, a teiva and a flood, there are today, so every Jew must build a teiva with more learning and more kavanah, for time is short. He ties Moshe's teiva and the daughter of Pharaoh to the Zohar's 'bas malka' in every word of Torah and tefillah, and stresses that every Jew is precious and a hidden treasure.

title.en: A teiva big enough for every Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah, when the dearness of every Jew is revealed, and says Hashem calls even a far-off Jew 'my son'. He concludes that every Jew must build a teiva big enough for all Jews, through Torah, tefillah and the Shabbos meals that save from Gog and Magog, since the nations make no distinction between Jews, and all will share the salvation.

catalogTitle: The Power of Man to Build or Destroy the World

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that man controls the whole world for good or for bad, and that Noach, damaged by Cham's sin in the Teva, was saved only out of mercy and in the merit of Avraham Avinu.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Midrash that Noach found chein, undeserved favor, and was saved because Avraham Avinu would descend from him, and asks why the Zichronos of Rosh Hashanah praise Hashem for remembering Noach if his rescue was planned from the start. Through Rashi's account that the lion maimed Noach, the dispute over the lion's food, and Rashi's covenant that kept the food fresh, he builds his answer. Man controls the world by remote control: before Adam's sin the world was a peaceful utopia, and human sin corrupted even the animals. The Mabul was to restart the world with a society of tzaddikim, but Cham sinned in the Teva and affected Noach, so the lion needed meat and attacked him. Noach was saved only in Avraham's merit. The Mashgiach concludes that today Jews who learn and keep the Torah carry the fate of the world, and the real front of the war is in the beis medrash.

en: Chein means undeserved favor: according to the Midrash Noach was saved not by his own merit but because Avraham Avinu would descend from him.
Man controls the entire world by remote control: his mitzvos bring peace and bounty, and his sins bring war, hunger and corruption, even among the animals.
The Mabul was meant to start the world anew from a society of tzaddikim, people and animals alike, in the state of the world before Adam's sin.
Cham's sin in the Teva affected Noach and spoiled the plan, so the lion needed meat, attacked Noach, and no miracle protected him.
Since Avraham Avinu, only Jews control the world, and Jews who learn Torah and do mitzvos decide whether it has peace or war.
Teshuvah can still change the decree after Yom Kippur, as the rain at the start of the Mabul could have turned into rain of blessing.

title.en: Noach's undeserved favor and the Zichronos

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that chein means undeserved favor and that Noach was saved because Avraham Avinu would descend from him. He then asks why the Zichronos of Rosh Hashanah single out Hashem's remembering Noach with kindness, if Noach's rescue was programmed from the start.

title.en: The lion that maimed Noach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi that Noach was maimed by the lion when he was late with its food, and asks why Hashem, who made so many miracles in the Teva, did not help him feed it on time. He brings the Ibn Ezra that the lion ate straw, against Chazal that each animal got its own diet, and Rashi that a covenant kept all the food from spoiling.

title.en: Man controls the world by remote control

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the world before the Mabul as a utopia and explains that Adam's sin contaminated it, because man controls the world for good or bad. Human corruption grew until even the animals sinned, and he brings Yeshayahu and the Ramban on Bechukosai that in the days of Moshiach animals will again not prey on each other.

title.en: Starting over with a society of tzaddikim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem decided to wipe out the world and start over from a nucleus of tzaddikim. Every person has a portion of the world that his deeds affect; Noach's portion, Eretz Yisrael, was not flooded, and the animals of his portion stayed pure and came to the Teva, where, as before the sin, the lions needed no meat.

title.en: Cham's sin and Noach's wine

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Sanhedrin that Cham, the dog and the raven broke the rules of the Teva, and explains that Cham's sin affected his father Noach, as a sin spreads to generations before and after. This is why Noach did not realize he could not drink wine as one will in the days of Moshiach, and he became drunk.

title.en: Saved only in the merit of Avraham

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that after Cham's sin the lion was no longer satisfied with straw, attacked Noach and maimed him, and Hashem made no miracle for a sinful society. By the condition of the Teva Noach should have perished, but he was saved out of mercy because Avraham Avinu would come from him; this answers the opening question and the Zichronos, and the parsha, which starts with Noach and ends with Avraham, is like a headline.

title.en: The war is fought in the beis medrash

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem put all of creation under man's control, and after giving the nations several chances He chose Avraham, so that today only Jews who know what Hashem wants are responsible for the world. The war of the day, he says, is fought in the batei medrash where Jews learn and daven, and he brings Rashi that the rain of the Mabul began as rain that could have been blessing, to show that even after Yom Kippur the decree can be changed.

title.en: A fateful year: Hoshana Rabbah, the moon and the soldiers

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the fate of the Jewish people rests on the shoulders of those who learn, especially in this year. He brings the tradition that the final war will begin on Hoshana Rabbah, notes that the war in Afghanistan began then on a moonlit night, brings the Rema and Ramban on the moon and the shadow on Hoshana Rabbah and the stars that fought Sisera, and calls Yishmael a pere adam who can be fought only with Torah and mitzvos.

catalogTitle: כי אותך ראיתי צדיק לפני בדור הזה - חיזוק לדור האחרון

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem told Noach "I have seen you as a tzaddik before Me in this generation" to strengthen him, and that every Jew in the last generation, living in a world like the flood, must hear these words as said to himself and hide in the ark of Torah and tefillah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the image of the material world as a flood and the word of Torah and tefillah as the ark. He asks why Hashem paid Noach a compliment, which is not His way. Through the Satmar Rav's question on Rashi's two readings of "in his generations", the Arizal's words to R' Chaim Vital and Sefer Chassidim, he shows that Hashem measures a person by what he could have been without his generation's obstacles. Noach, seeing himself smaller than earlier generations, needed this chizuk. The Mashgiach describes the Nefilim who fell and made others fall, the polluted atmosphere of the flood, and today's even greater pollution, and teaches that the ark today is Torah, tefillah and Tehillim, with Hashem holding a Jew's hand. He connects this to Marcheshvan and the lulav, to the raven and the Jews who waited in the darkness in Egypt, and to Yeshayahu's call to hide, and closes that each Jew must take the words "ki oscha ra'isi tzaddik" as chizuk.

en: Hashem praised Noach as a tzaddik in his generation to strengthen him, because Noach saw himself as smaller than the earlier generations and had fallen in his own eyes.
Hashem measures a person not by what he is but by the generation he lives in and what he could have been without its obstacles.
The world of the flood was polluted by the Nefilim, who fell and made others fall, and today's world is more polluted than ever, so serving Hashem is very hard.
The only rescue is to hide in Torah and tefillah, the ark of today, and to know that Hashem holds a Jew's hand even at the end of the long sea of exile.
The holiness of Tishrei, like the Name of Hashem drawn into the lulav's movements, must be brought back to the heart and carried through the whole year.
Noach waited in the ark, and the Jews waited in Egypt during the darkness, until Hashem commanded them to leave; salvation must come from Hashem, not through means against the Torah.
In today's generation, every Jew must say to himself that Hashem tells him "ki oscha ra'isi tzaddik", since this is a time for chizuk rather than for humility.

title.en: The ark of a luminous word; Cheshvan's Yom Tov

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains "make a light for the ark" as making each word of tefillah and Torah fiery and luminous, since the material world is a flood and the word is the ark that saves from it. He then says Cheshvan has no Yom Tov of its own; its Yom Tov is Torah, and the generation of the flood was meant to receive the Torah but it turned into rain.

title.en: Why Hashem complimented Noach

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Hashem told Noach "I have seen you as a tzaddik before Me", since Hashem does not give compliments except after a test, as with Avraham after the Akeidah. He brings the Satmar Rav's question on Rashi's reading of "in his generations" to Noach's discredit, and begins the story of the Arizal telling R' Chaim Vital that his soul was higher than the Tannaim.

title.en: Measured by the generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Sefer Chassidim and the Chida that Hashem measures a person by his generation, so a small person who serves Hashem in a corrupt time is greater than a great one of an earlier time. He applies this to Noach: both of Rashi's readings say the same thing, and the discredit is the generation's, which held Noach back from reaching Avraham's level.

title.en: Noach's chizuk; the Nefilim who made others fall

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Noach, comparing himself to the earlier generations whose levels kept declining, fell in his own eyes, so Hashem strengthened him by measuring him against what he could have been. He then explains the Nefilim as angels who fell and, by the form of the word, made others fall too, polluting the atmosphere of the world.

title.en: A world cut off from its root

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a polluted place prevents tefillah, as Moshe had to leave the city of Egypt to daven. In Noach's time the corruption went so deep that even animals left their kind and were cut off from their root, as robbery cuts a person from his root. He says today's world is more polluted than ever and that earlier tzaddikim said serving Hashem before Moshiach will be very hard.

title.en: Living with Parshas Noach today

summary.en: The Mashgiach says each Jew must identify with Parshas Noach and hear Hashem's words to Noach as said to him. Moshe was shown "until the last day", the great sea of the end of days in which only a few are saved in the ark of Torah and tefillah, and he describes today's media that bring impurity to everyone. The only advice is to hide in Torah and tefillah and know that Hashem is with us.

title.en: Tehillim: Your right hand holds me

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the chapter of Tehillim that wherever a person goes, even to the end of the sea, Hashem's hand leads him, and the verse "You hold my right hand, You guide me with Your counsel". He says to strengthen the ark with more Torah, tefillah and Tehillim, citing Mesilas Yesharim on Tehillim, and that each blatt Gemara and chapter of Tehillim is counsel for surviving the flood.

title.en: Marcheshvan and the lulav's Name of Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings R' Yisrael of Kozhnitz that Marcheshvan comes from lips that still murmur the tefillos of Tishrei. He explains that the four minim form Hashem's Name, and the na'anuim draw it down and bring it back to the chest, so that Hashem stays at one's right side and before him; the knowledge that Hashem is everywhere must be brought from the mind into the heart.

title.en: Carrying the sukkah all year

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why one longs for the lulav and sukkah when Sukkos ends: the four minim and Hashem's Name are in the Sefer Torah, which is why Simchas Torah follows. He brings the Yismach Moshe's dream in which an angel told him that the Tanna is not in Gan Eden but Gan Eden is in the Tanna, and concludes that one attached to Torah carries the sukkah with him all year; this is the meaning of Marcheshvan.

title.en: Noach's chen versus the flood generation's beauty

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a Slonimer teaching on "and Noach found favor in Hashem's eyes": the generation of the flood sought chen in physical beauty, mixing angelic beauty with the body, while Noach found chen in hoping for Hashem's kindness. He adds that today a film of foolishness covers the Gemara, and one must ask Hashem to see its life.

title.en: Waiting for the command: the raven and the darkness

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Noach did not leave the ark until Hashem told him to, which was his test, and the Chazal of the raven that refused Noach's mission and was kept for another mission, feeding Eliyahu. He brings the Toras Moshe on "He sent darkness and they did not rebel against His word": during the darkness the Jews could have fled Egypt, but they waited for Hashem's command, unlike the children of Ephraim who left early and were killed.

title.en: The raven's hint to Noach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Noach, exhausted from caring for the creatures in the ark, sent the raven to learn whether the flood had ended. The raven's refusal hinted that it was destined to serve Eliyahu, the herald of the redemption, and that one must wait until Hashem sends the salvation and not seek it through means against the Torah; Noach understood and stayed until Hashem said "go out of the ark".

title.en: Hide in your rooms until the wrath passes

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Yeshayahu's call "go, My people, come into your rooms" as Hashem's message in exile: hide in the beis medrash and the sukkah of Torah, because the outside atmosphere is contagious. He contrasts the ghettos of the past with today's open society that seeks to absorb the Jews, and brings the Arizal that the generation of the flood returned in the generation of the dispersion, Sodom and Egypt, all of whose souls come together today to be rectified.

title.en: Not a time for humility: "I have seen you as a tzaddik"

summary.en: The Mashgiach says today's world repeats the flood's sins, citing the Midrash that the flood generation wrote marriage contracts between men, and now such things are legalized. He calls for combining Gemara with Tehillim and Chumash, and concludes that every Jew today is very great, must hear Hashem saying "ki oscha ra'isi tzaddik" to him, and needs chizuk rather than humility, unlike Avraham who needed no support.

catalogTitle: התשובה והתיקון של נח ודורו - "מחני נא מספרך"

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Noach failed to pray for his generation because he did not include himself among them with mesiras nefesh, and that his teshuvah after the flood, admitting that only Hashem can save a person from the yetzer hara, turned the very reason for the flood into the reason there would never be another.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach asks why Noach did not pray for his generation. Rabbeinu Bachya answers that there were not ten tzaddikim, yet the Midrash and Zohar fault Noach, calling the flood 'the waters of Noach'. The Mashgiach reconciles them: without ten tzaddikim prayer cannot help, but mesiras nefesh can, by including oneself among the sinners, as Moshe did with 'mecheini na' and by breaking the luchos. Avraham was not allowed such self-sacrifice, so he prayed instead. Through Kayin's 'hashomer achi anochi', Eliyahu's words and the Gemara's teaching that man the damager is defined by teshuvah, the Mashgiach shows that the deepest teshuvah is admitting that Hashem created the yetzer hara and begging Him for help. Noach did this after the flood, so 'the inclination of man's heart is evil' became the reason not to bring another flood. He adds why the animals perished, why Eretz Yisrael was spared, and that the teivah is the word of Torah and tefillah.

en: Without ten tzaddikim prayer cannot save a generation, but mesiras nefesh, including oneself among the sinners, can, and this is what was demanded of Noach.
Moshe Rabbeinu repaired Noach's failing with 'mecheini na misifrecha' and by breaking the luchos, declaring himself no better than the sinners.
The greatest teshuvah is to recognize that Hashem created the yetzer hara and to beg Him to save one from it, as in the Yom Kippur prayer that one not sin again.
Man as man never damages; his defining trait as a damager is his ability to make a tikkun through teshuvah, which is why 'adam hamazik' is learned from a verse about repentance.
A person's possessions are an extension of his soul, so the damage his animal does reflects his own middos.
After the flood Noach admitted that only Hashem can help against the yetzer hara, so the same verse that justified the flood became the reason never to bring another.
The teivah is the word of Torah and tefillah, the refuge from today's flood; if one cannot daven or learn, one must make a cheshbon hanefesh.

title.en: Why Noach did not pray for his generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Noach did not pray for his generation and brings Rabbeinu Bachya's answer that there were not ten tzaddikim. He contrasts the Midrash, where Hashem rebukes Noach for complaining only after the destruction, and the Zohar, which calls the flood 'the waters of Noach' and says Moshe Rabbeinu came as his tikkun.

title.en: 'Mecheini na': mesiras nefesh for the generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Moshe's 'mecheini na' repaired 'mei Noach', and resolves the contradiction: without ten tzaddikim prayer cannot help, but mesiras nefesh, including oneself among the sinners, can. He brings the Midrash that Moshe broke the luchos to say he too had sinned, and concludes that this was demanded of Noach.

title.en: Avraham, prayer and the korban

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why Avraham, who gave himself up in Ur Kasdim, did not break idols in Canaan: Hashem had promised to make him a great nation, so he was not allowed mesiras nefesh. Therefore Hashem revealed Sodom's fate to him so that he would pray, and the Mashgiach adds that a korban is itself a form of mesiras nefesh, which is why Noach's korban brought an eis ratzon.

title.en: One verse as reason for and against the flood

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that nefilas apayim was a danger the great tzaddikim accepted with mesiras nefesh. He then raises the difficulty that 'the inclination of man's heart is evil' is given both as the reason for the flood and, after Noach's korban, as the reason not to bring another, cites the Baal HaTanya, and opens the Gemara's teaching that 'mav'eh' means man, learned from 'im tiv'ayun be'ayu'.

title.en: Kayin's 'Am I my brother's keeper' as teshuvah

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that no word in the Torah is a lie and explains Kayin's 'hashomer achi anochi' with a mashal of a thief who asks the watchman why he let him steal. Like Eliyahu, who 'spoke harshly toward Above', Kayin meant that Hashem created the yetzer hara and alone can guard from it, which the Mashgiach calls the greatest teshuvah, as in the Yom Kippur prayer. He then applies it to Noach, who should have said he was no better than his generation.

title.en: Adam hamazik and the power of tikkun

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that man as man never damages; what damages in him is the animal soul. Adam hamazik is therefore described by 'im tiv'ayun be'ayu', a verse of teshuvah, since only man can make a tikkun; this is also why Hashem said 'ketz kol basar ba lefanai'. He adds that in heaven a sin is mentioned only through its tikkun, and that a human damager, unlike an animal, must make whole every aspect of the harm.

title.en: Property as an extension of the soul

summary.en: Based on the Ba'al Shem Tov, the Mashgiach teaches that a person's property is an extension of his soul, as with Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's donkey that would not eat untithed food. This is why an owner pays for his animal's damage: had he been a proper person, free of anger and loshon hara, it would not have damaged. A goring ox comes from the owner himself, and when it has gored three times he should, with a broken heart, throw himself before Hashem for help.

title.en: Noach's teshuvah turns the reason around

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to Noach: after leaving the teivah and seeing the destruction he spoke like Kayin, attributing the yetzer hara to Hashem and admitting he was helpless and had been saved only by Hashem's help. The generation of the flood never admitted they needed Hashem, so their yetzer hara brought the flood; after Noach's admission the existence of the yetzer hara became the reason for mercy.

title.en: Why the animals perished: the Yismach Moshe

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the animals died in the flood if only man sinned, and brings the Yismach Moshe: the ten generations from Adam to Noach kept angering Hashem, their souls were reincarnated in animals, plants and even the earth, and kept sinning there, so everything had to be erased. The fish, which held souls of tzaddikim, were spared, and he connects this to the tikkun of souls through eating fish on Shabbos.

title.en: The world given to man; Noach's portion

summary.en: The Mashgiach adds that 'the earth He gave to man': each person has a portion of creation, and his deeds affect it, as Mesilas Yesharim teaches. The generation of the flood ruined all of creation, while the animals bound to Noach's soul came with him into the teivah, and Eretz Yisrael, which the Mashgiach suggests was Noach's portion, was not flooded.

title.en: Today's flood and the teivah of the word

summary.en: The Mashgiach draws the lesson that man bears great responsibility: the world today is polluted because people are, and if people were good the world would be good. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov that the teivah is the word of tefillah and Torah, the refuge in today's stormy sea; if one cannot daven or learn something is wrong, and 'the Name of Hashem is a tower of strength' to run into.

title.en: Eretz Yisrael held by servants; a new world with Avraham

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rabbeinu Bachya that Hashem gave Eretz Yisrael to Canaan, a servant, to guard it, since a servant cannot acquire it, and suggests the same of the Yishmaelim after the churban. He closes that the parsha ends with the birth of Avraham Avinu, a new world, and every Jew should identify with it, place himself under Hashem's protection, and ask for a pure heart.

catalogTitle: דור המבול ודור הפלגה - האם אנחנו מתקנים חטאם?

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the souls of the generations of the Flood and the Dispersion keep returning to be repaired, and that Parshas Noach calls on each Jew to ask whether he has fixed their flaws, through good middos and through Torah learned with inner light.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the passuk 'binu shnos dor vador', which Chazal read as a command to contemplate the generations of the Flood and the Dispersion. Citing the Arizal, he explains that their souls returned in Mitzrayim and again and again, and asks whether we have repaired them: the Flood generation legalized immorality, and its flaw was bad middos. A story of jealousy at a wedding and an incident in shul illustrate this. He then explains a person's power to build or ruin creation, why Noach's portion and Eretz Yisrael were spared, and how the Flood was the outer form of a Torah the generation refused, later given through Moshe, Noach's reincarnation. Parshas Noach continues the protective sukkah of Tishrei: the teivah, like the sukkah, is built of Hashem's names. Today, without great tzaddikim, one must run into the 'teivah', the luminous word of Torah and tefillah, and work on good middos.

en: The command 'binu shnos dor vador' means contemplating the Flood and Dispersion generations, whose souls return in every era to be repaired.
The Flood generation's main flaw was bad middos, and its worst step was turning sin into law and culture.
Every person controls a portion of creation and can build or destroy it with his deeds; Noach's portion, his animals and Eretz Yisrael, did not sin and was spared.
The Torah was meant to descend in Noach's time; the Flood generation refused it, so only its outer form came down as the forty days of rain.
Parshas Noach extends the protection of the Tishrei sukkah: the teivah, like the sukkah, shields because it is built of halachos, the names of Hashem.
Today, without the great tzaddikim who protected the world, a Jew must run into the 'teivah', the word of Torah and tefillah, and make it luminous.

inner and outer Torah (pnimiyus and chitzoniyus)
Shemini Atzeres and the rain of Torah
Shimon HaTzaddik and the world's foundations

title.en: Binu shnos dor vador: who were these generations?

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the command to contemplate 'the years of each generation', which Chazal apply to the Flood and Dispersion generations. Citing the Arizal, he says their souls returned in Mitzrayim and received the Torah, and asks whether we, too, are still those souls who have not yet improved.

title.en: The sins: bad middos made into law

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the Flood generation, sunk in physicality and bad middos, with the over-clever Dispersion generation that wanted to storm heaven. He stresses the Midrash that the Flood generation wrote immorality into law, compares this to legalized evils today, and says derech eretz comes before Torah: one must ask whether one is like them or like Noach.

title.en: The jealous man at the wedding; the souls return again

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a shoemaker in Lita who grew rich and made a fine wedding, where a jealous man shamed him at the chuppah, and of Rav Yisrael Salanter's saying that the rabbonim would answer for not teaching mussar. He then lists how these souls returned, in Mitzrayim and in Korach's band, and asks whether after all the floods of the generations we have finally repaired our middos.

title.en: An incident in shul and the duty to learn the parsha

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes a Rosh Chodesh incident in a shul where the congregation hounded the man who had opened the aron, and asks whether we are cleansed of the Flood generation's middos. He says the task of repairing it lasts until Moshiach, traces the sins back to Kayin, and urges a special effort this week to learn the parsha in depth with Ramban, Targum Yonasan, Rabbeinu Bachya and the Midrashim.

title.en: Man's power over creation; Noach's portion

summary.en: Based on Derech Hashem and Nefesh HaChaim, the Mashgiach explains that a person with a G-dly soul controls creation: each limb and sinew is a button connected to the worlds, building through mitzvos and destroying through sins. Until the Dispersion all people had this power; the Flood generation corrupted even the animals. Noach's portion, the animals that came to the ark and Eretz Yisrael, did not sin and was not flooded.

title.en: The Torah refused by the Flood generation; Noach and Moshe

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that at Matan Torah the nations feared a new flood, and the Gemara deriving Moshe from 'beshagam'. He explains with the Midrash that Hashem wished to give the Flood generation the Torah and they refused, and with the Zohar that Noach, who fell and did not pray for his generation, was reincarnated as Moshe, who gave himself for his generation and received the Torah.

title.en: Inner and outer: rain and Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that everything has an inner and an outer side, and that the Torah is called water. Bringing the Chasam Sofer and the Midrash on grain, wine and oil, he says that on Shemini Atzeres one asks for the inner side of rain, which is Torah. In Noach's time the Torah came down only in its outer form, the forty days and nights of rain, since the generation did not want its inner side.

title.en: Matan Torah under the stars of the Flood

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that at Matan Torah the heavenly configuration matched that of the Flood, so the nations expected a flood; the answer was that a triple Torah was coming, which, as the Maharal explains of the letter shin, endures rather than destroys. The Flood generation received only the outer side, while Matan Torah brought down the hidden treasure, the inner Torah.

title.en: Tishrei builds a sukkah of protection

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the whole work of Tishrei is to build a sukkah, a place of protection from evil forces. With the Ba'al HaTanya's siddur on 'bakeseh l'yom chageinu' he shows that the sukkah is built from Rosh Hashanah on. Like the sukkos in which Klal Yisrael sat even in battle, the sukkah is a spiritual shield of bitachon, and its protection goes with a Jew all year, which is the joy of Shemini Atzeres.

title.en: The teivah as a sukkah of Hashem's names

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that Parshas Noach, the first Shabbos after Tishrei, gives a new sukkah: the teivah, a flimsy box of wood and pitch that withstood the boiling waters. A sukkah protects because it is made of halachos, the names of Hashem, as 'migdal oz shem Hashem'. He brings the gematria of sukkah and shows that the ark's dimensions also spell Hashem's name.

title.en: Parshas Noach extends Sukkos; Noach himself was the shelter

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that when Tishrei ends, learning Parshas Noach in depth carries its sukkah and its Shemini Atzeres rain of Torah into the year, since the Torah is eternal. With 'sar tzilam' and Rashi he explains that the tzaddik is the shade of his generation, and with the Yismach Moshe's dream, that the Gan Eden was inside the Tanna, he concludes that Noach did not enter the teivah: the teivah was in Noach.

title.en: Without our tzaddikim: Torah, avodah, chesed

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that earlier generations had great tzaddikim who sheltered the world, such as the Satmar Rav, and now we are left alone and must run to the teivah, the word, explained by the Ba'al Shem Tov's 'tzohar ta'aseh lateivah'. He explains Shimon HaTzaddik's saying as the last of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah: the world stands not on them but on Torah, avodah and gemilus chasadim, and so one must now take these on, learning and davening with light.

title.en: Pnimiyus, good middos and running into the teivah

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that one must learn and daven with pnimiyus and have good middos, which are no contradiction to being a talmid chacham or a chassid; the Chumash records the Flood generation's bad middos, the preparation they lacked for Torah. He closes with Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz's reading of the Ba'al Shem Tov: today's world is a flood, and one is saved only by running into the luminous teivah, the Gemara, Chumash and Tehillim, and ends with a tefillah.

catalogTitle: The Creation and Necessity of the Jewish Nation

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that with Avraham Avinu a new species came into the world, the Jew who believes in Hashem by inherited instinct, and that the Jewish nation exists because it must, not because of anyone's merit.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by calling Avraham the purpose of creation and the start of a new species. He asks why emunah is written as a statement, not a command, and contrasts the Rambam with the Ramban. Knowledge, he explains, is acquired, but some knowledge is inherited, like the beaver's dam or the spider's web. Every human can see Hashem in the wonders of the body, but a Jew believes by instinct, as the Chasam Sofer's case of a father and son shows. Avraham, the first believer, was a new creation: hence the miracle of his children, his exemption from honoring his father, and his call to Eretz Yisrael, the first land. The Mashgiach then asks why the Ramban says Avraham sinned by going to Mitzrayim, and why the Torah never tells his merits. Using the Maharal and the Midrash Tanchuma, he answers that the Jewish nation had to exist, and that Avraham went down to prepare his children's purity there.

en: With Avraham Avinu a new species was created: the Jew, for whom the purpose of all creation exists.
Belief in Hashem is for a Jew an inherited instinct, like the instinctive skills of animals, passed down from Avraham.
A Jew can spoil this inborn emunah through aveiros, especially forbidden food and immorality, just as a body is spoiled by abuse, and it can be healed.
Avraham, the man of the beginning, belongs in Eretz Yisrael, the land where creation began.
The Torah does not state Avraham's merits because the Jewish nation must exist regardless of anyone's deserving.
Avraham went down to Mitzrayim to prepare the ground for his children, whose purity there came from Sarah's and Yosef's steadfastness.
