title.en: Avraham the new creation; emunah as a statement

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Avraham the purpose of creation and the beginning of a new Jewish species. He then notes that the mitzvah of emunah is written as a statement, not a command, and brings the Rambam who counts it and the Ramban who calls it the foundation before the mitzvos.

title.en: Acquired knowledge and inherited knowledge

summary.en: The Mashgiach distinguishes knowledge acquired from outside from knowledge that is inherited, with the beaver's dam, the spider's web, the migrating bird and the nursing infant. He concludes that a Jew knows Hashem in the same inherited way, passed down from Avraham, the father of believers.

title.en: The wonders of the human body

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the nations are held to account for not believing in one G-d: a person can see Hashem in his own body. He describes an anatomy book he once read, and the wonders of the spine, the eye and the interdependent systems of the body, concluding that a Jew, besides this understanding, believes by instinct.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer: the instinct of belonging

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer's case of a son whose thief father breaks in without knowing it is his son's house: the son may not kill him, since a father instinctively will not kill his son. He links this to the passuk that the ox knows its owner, and says Jews, as children of Hashem, know Him by instinct.

title.en: The first believer; spoiling and healing emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the word emunah first appears with Avraham, and calls the Jew a species that believes by heredity. Like a stomach ruined by bad food or a clogged heart, this spiritual organism can be spoiled by aveiros, above all forbidden food and immorality, and then needs treatment.

title.en: Avraham, a species of his own

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the morning passage that lists all of creation and then adds 'You chose Avram', as the item still missing. Because Avraham was a new species, not a link in the chain from Adam and Noach, he and Sarah needed a miracle to have children, and he was exempt from honoring his father. This is the third creation in Bereishis.

title.en: The first Jew in the first land

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains 'Lech lecha' as sending the first Jew to Eretz Yisrael, the first place created, from which the world developed. He shows that the Torah's first passuk and first word, and the first haftarah, point to Eretz Yisrael, and that Hashem's first words to Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov all concern the land, matching Avraham's chesed and Yitzchak's din.

title.en: The Ramban: Avraham's sin in going to Mitzrayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ramban that Avraham sinned by going down to Mitzrayim and exposing Sarah to Pharaoh, and that the exile in Mitzrayim was its punishment. Citing Rabbeinu Yonah that a tzaddik must be judged favorably even beyond reason, he asks why the Ramban did not find a merit for Avraham.

title.en: The Maharal: a Jew's sin is only on the surface

summary.en: The Mashgiach introduces the Maharal, who taught that a Jew is fundamentally a tzaddik and his aveira is only on the surface, like soot on a chimney sweep that washes off. A gentile's sin comes from his nature and stays; therefore teshuvah is for a Jew.

title.en: Why the Torah does not introduce Avraham

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Torah opens Noach by calling him a tzaddik, but begins Lech Lecha with Hashem's call to Avraham without saying why he deserved it. He recounts from the Midrashim how Avraham defied Nimrod, was thrown into the fire and saved, and only then received his first prophecy.

title.en: The Maharal on Moshe's unnamed parents

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Maharal on why the Torah introduces Moshe's parents only as 'a man of the house of Levi': the redemption is absolute and does not depend on anyone's merit. He applies this to Avraham: the Torah does not give his merits because the world was created for the Jewish nation, which had to exist.

title.en: The Midrash Tanchuma: it had to be

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Avraham, as a prophet, knew his children would go to Mitzrayim. He brings the Midrash Tanchuma in Vayeshev that Adam had to eat from the Etz HaDaas, that the Jews had to go to Mitzrayim, that Yosef had to be sold and that Moshe could not enter Eretz Yisrael, all as part of Hashem's plan.

title.en: Preparing purity in Mitzrayim; the Ramban's intent

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Avraham went down to prepare the ground: Sarah's purity in Pharaoh's house brought holiness to the Jewish women in Mitzrayim, as Yosef's did for the men. The Ramban knew the Zohar's merit for Avraham but wrote that he sinned to teach that Hashem's choice of the Jewish nation does not rest on merit: the nation must exist and is fundamentally pure.

catalogTitle: המקוה והתיבה הם כמו embassy של שמים על הארץ

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the mikveh, like Noach's teivah and the sukkah, is a piece of heaven on earth, an embassy of Shamayim where judgment is sweetened at its root and evil cannot follow.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the different wording of Noach's missions to the raven and the dove: the raven is a taker, the dove, likened to Knesses Yisrael, a giver. He then asks why Rabbi Yehuda in the Haggadah gives simanim for the makos, and ties it to his view that chametz is removed only by burning. The answer rests on sweetening judgment at its root: Noach's korban reached the root, so the yetzer hara that brought the flood became the reason for no more flood, and a unanimous Sanhedrin acquits for the same reason. The four ways of removing chametz match the four elements of Shem Havaya, with fire, Yehuda's element, as the root. From there he explains the mikveh as fire within water, an embassy of heaven on earth, like the sukkah and the teivah, and closes on immersing beyond obligation, with stories of tzaddikim.

en: The raven, a taker, would keep coming back to Noach while food was still bitter, while the dove, a giver, would not return once it could find any livelihood at all.
Judgment is sweetened at its root: Noach's korban reached the root of creation, where the same reason that demanded the flood demanded that there be no more flood.

The four ways of removing chametz correspond to the four elements, which come from the four letters of Shem Havaya; fire is the root of them all, and Rabbi Yehuda, linked to Yehuda and to fire, holds that only burning removes chametz.
The mikveh is a piece of heaven on earth: heaven is fire and water, and the mikveh's water holds the element of fire, so whoever enters it is in a place where evil does not exist.
Like an embassy where a country's police may not enter, the mikveh, the sukkah and Noach's teivah are places of heaven where earthly decrees do not apply.
Though Ezra's enactment requiring tevilah was annulled, one who loves Hashem does more than the obligation, as Mesilas Yesharim describes the trait of chassidus.

candidateTopics: Rabbi Yehuda's simanim in the Haggadah

title.en: The raven and the dove: taker and giver

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Torah describes the raven's mission and the dove's mission differently, and explains that the raven, cruel even to its own young, is a taker who would keep returning to Noach, while the dove, likened to Knesses Yisrael, prefers bitter food of its own to taking.

title.en: Rabbi Yehuda's simanim and burning chametz

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that saying the makos at the Seder draws plagues on Israel's enemies and healing on Israel, and asks what Rabbi Yehuda's simanim come to add. He then brings the Mishnah's dispute on removing chametz, where Rabbi Yehuda holds it is done only by burning.

title.en: Sweetening judgment at its root: Noach's korban

summary.en: The Mashgiach introduces the principle that judgment is sweetened at its root, and shows it in the parsha: the yetzer hara is the reason given both for the flood and for the promise of no more flood, because Noach's korban brought a nachas ruach that reached the root of creation, where din turns into chesed.

title.en: Unanimous Sanhedrin, Tishrei and Nissan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why a Sanhedrin that unanimously convicts lets the accused go free: each sage receives Torah through his own channel, like water in colored glass, and unanimity shows they reached the colorless root where chayav turns to zakai. He adds that Tishrei and Nissan, the roots of time, are when evil is nullified, through teshuvah and through removing chametz.

title.en: Four elements, four ways, and Yehuda as fire

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the world was created from the four letters of Shem Havaya, which are the four elements; removing one element dissolves a thing, so the four ways of removing chametz each use one element. Fire is the root of all four, corresponding to Yehuda, the leading tribe, whose degel was under Gavriel, and Rabbi Yehuda is a gilgul of Yehuda.

title.en: Burning at the root and the simanim answered

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that Rabbi Yehuda, standing for fire, wants chametz uprooted from its very root, and from the root one can sweeten judgment. Haggadah means drawing down, like a gid, and the more makos found the greater the salvation; Rabbi Yehuda's simanim, in line with his view, go to the root to draw healing for Israel, as on Rosh Hashanah with its many references to fire.

title.en: The mikveh of fire and the mikveh of water

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that whatever exists below exists above, and the heavenly mikveh is the Nehar Dinur, a river of fire. Since people cannot immerse in fire, Hashem joined fire with water; heaven itself is fire and water, and the mikveh's forty se'ah reflect Shem Havaya, four letters and ten in its filled spelling, so Mikveh Yisrael is Hashem.

title.en: The mikveh as heaven's embassy

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the mikveh removes evil: it is heaven, where evil does not dwell. Like a spy fleeing into a foreign embassy where he cannot be touched, a Jew pursued by impurity or illness flees into Hashem's embassy, which is why tzaddikim went to the mikveh with tefillah; there breathing stops and he emerges a new person.

title.en: Sukkah, teivah and the holy names

summary.en: The Mashgiach extends the idea to the sukkah, built by halachos that are holy names, into which Yaakov fled from Esav, and to Noach's teivah, which had to follow its halachos so that the decree of the flood did not apply to those inside. He brings the Yalkut Reuveni that the teivah's dimensions are Shem Havaya, and the Targum that Haman's fifty-amah beam came from the teivah.

title.en: Kavanas haMikveh: rebirth through bitul

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the halachos of mikveh are holy names, and reads from the Kavanas haMikveh in the Ba'al HaTanya's siddur: at creation the earth lay beneath the water, and man, who is from the earth, returns through tevilah to his root and is created anew, provided he immerses with bitul to Hashem. He adds the Reishis Chochmah that the mikveh is the World to Come, like Noach's teivah.

title.en: Why immerse when it is not required

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why one should immerse when Ezra's enactment of tevilah was annulled, and answers from Mesilas Yesharim's chapter on chassidus: a son who loves his father does what he hints at, not only what he commands. Hashem loves purity, as seen in the Beis HaMikdash, korbanos, the regel and Matan Torah, for which Moshe added a day so that Israel would be pure.

title.en: Benayahu on the snowy day

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Benayahu ben Yehoyada broke the ice to immerse on a snowy day so he could learn, centuries before Ezra's enactment, showing self-sacrifice for purity beyond obligation. He cites Rav Hai Gaon and Rabbeinu Chananel and the saying of Rabbi Aharon HaGadol that mikveh is not a mitzvah, yet nothing brings to mitzvos like it.

title.en: Stories of tzaddikim and the mikveh

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Slonimer chassid who sensed that meat came from a shochet who had not gone to the mikveh, of a Lechovitcher chassid who immersed in a Moscow river before onlookers and was greeted by Rabbi Mordechai of Lechovitch, of Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan going to the mikveh over a difficult question, and of Rabbi Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld's answer to Rabbi Isser Zalman Meltzer.

title.en: Hashem as the mikveh, and closing wishes

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Arizal and the Shelah on tevilah for a pure heart, notes that Hashem cleansed the world with the waters of the flood, and that Hashem Himself is the mikveh and the source of living water, the opposite of kareis. He closes by wishing that the warmth of Sukkos continue through the mikveh, and that learning and davening be done in purity.

catalogTitle: התיבה היתה צריך להיות עולם התיקון אלא שחם קלקול אותה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the ark was meant to be the seed of a renewed world of tikkun, free of decay and predation, and that Cham's sin inside it spoiled the plan, so Noach was remembered only for the sake of Avraham Avinu.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Midrash that Noach found favor for the sake of his offspring, and with the Chasam Sofer's reading that the 'tzaddik tamim' of the opening verse is Avraham Avinu. He asks why the parsha first says 'tzaddik tamim in his generations' and later only 'tzaddik in this generation', and why Hashem's remembering Noach, the first verse of Zichronos, counts as great love. He then raises the questions about the ark: its size, feeding every creature, the lion that struck Noach, food that did not spoil. He explains that the bris prevented decay, which entered the world through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge. Hashem's plan was to restart the world of tikkun from Noach's righteous share of creation, where even the lion ate straw. Cham's sin ruined this; the lion again needed meat. Noach was saved only for Avraham. He closes that Cheshvan, after Tishrei, can still be turned around through teshuvah.

en: Noach was saved from the flood for the sake of his offspring, above all Avraham Avinu and the Jewish people.
Hashem created a world of tikkun with no decay, death or predation; the sin of the Tree of Knowledge brought decay, and in the days of Moshiach the original world will return.
The ark was meant to be a gathering of righteous creatures, Noach's own unspoiled portion of creation, from which Hashem would rebuild the world of tikkun.
Cham's sin in the ark nullified the plan: the creatures became mortal and spoiled again, and the lion became a predator that needed meat.
After the sin, by strict judgment the ark too should have been wiped out; Hashem remembered Noach with love only because Avraham would come from him.
Cheshvan, after the holy days of Tishrei, is like a flood for a Jew's personal world of tikkun, yet it can still be turned around through teshuvah.

candidateTopics: decay and the sin of the Tree of Knowledge

title.en: Noach saved for the sake of Avraham

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Noach found favor because of his offspring, and the Chasam Sofer, based on the Ibn Ezra's reckoning that Avraham was fifty-eight when Noach died, that the 'tzaddik tamim' of the opening verse is Avraham. He adds the Zera Kodesh's reading of the verse as an acronym for the Jewish people.

title.en: Two descriptions of Noach; Zichronos

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the parsha opens with 'tzaddik tamim in his generations' but later says only 'tzaddik in this generation'. He then turns to the Zichronos of Rosh Hashanah, whose first remembrance is Hashem's remembering Noach with love, and asks what great love there was in remembering Noach when saving him in the ark was the plan all along.

title.en: The lion's blow and the ark's capacity

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi that the word 'ach' in 'only Noach remained' means a lion struck Noach for bringing its food late. He then asks how the ark, three hundred amos long with three floors, could hold every species and how eight people could feed them all on schedule.

title.en: Miracles in the ark; the Ibn Ezra on meat

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rabbeinu Bachya that the ark was run by miracles, and asks what happened to the miracles on the day the lion's food was late. He cites the Ibn Ezra, who answers the question of meat for carnivores by saying they ate plants, and contrasts it with Chazal that Noach prepared each creature's own food.

title.en: The bris that prevents decay

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi that the covenant with Noach was so the food in the ark would not spoil, and explains that decay entered creation through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge, a breach of bris. Where there is bris nothing spoils: Yosef's grain and the body of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon.

title.en: Rebbe Elimelech's grave and a tzaddik's ink

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Jew he knew who was forced by the Nazis to open Rebbe Elimelech's grave in Lizhensk and saw him whole, and of a letter he owns whose signature stayed black. He concludes that Noach, the shomer habris, kept the ark's food from spoiling, so the Ibn Ezra's question never begins.

title.en: The world of tikkun and its return

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the world as Hashem created it, with people and animals that live forever and sing with the angels, and how Adam's sin brought decay. He brings Yeshayahu's prophecy that the lion will eat straw and the Ramban that in the days of Moshiach there will be no wild beasts, as at creation.

title.en: The ark as a new world from Noach's portion

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem wanted to wipe out the spoiled world and start anew from Noach. Every person owns a share of creation that his sins spoil; Noach's animals and his land, Eretz Yisrael, had not sinned, which is why the flood did not reach Eretz Yisrael, and the ark was a gathering of tzaddikim from which the world of tikkun would restart.

title.en: The lion ate straw until Cham sinned

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the lion in the ark, part of Noach's world of tikkun, ate straw, so Noach brought no meat, which answers the Ibn Ezra's question differently. Then Cham sinned in the ark, together with the raven and the dog, repeating Adam's breach of bris, and the plan of a new world was nullified.

title.en: Why the lion now needed meat

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a predator needs meat as concentrated food, while a tzaddik needs little, as Rashi says and as with Rabbi Nachum of Chernobyl. Once the ark's creatures were spoiled the lion needed meat, Noach had none, the straw came too late and the lion struck him; Hashem makes no miracles for sinful creatures, and Cham's sin reached back to Noach himself.

title.en: Remembered with love for Avraham's sake

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains 'only Noach remained' as a diminishing: the plan was undone, and by strict judgment the ark too should have been erased. Hashem remembered Noach with love because Avraham would come from him. This answers the opening question: 'tzaddik in this generation' was Hashem's word before the flood, while the parsha's opening, written by Moshe, points to Avraham, the tzaddik tamim.

title.en: Tishrei's tikkun and Cheshvan's flood

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that each year retells the story: Rosh Hashanah is the creation of a Jew's personal world of tikkun, and after the holy days comes a weekday world that floods it. Cheshvan, a dark month with no Yom Tov, is when parshas Noach is read, telling of Hashem's covenant and of remembering Noach for the sake of Avraham.

title.en: Turning the flood around through teshuvah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a Jew must believe he will yet become the Jew for whom the world was created, and that decrees can still be annulled until Chanukah, as the flood came down with mercy in Cheshvan. He shows that the very cause of the flood, the evil inclination, became the reason for the promise of no more flood, and closes that each person can at least repair his own world.

catalogTitle: מפרשת נח עד חנוכה הוא זמן לשוב בדרך רגילות בחיי יומית

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that from Parshas Noach until Zos Chanukah is the last time for teshuvah and the start of receiving the Torah in an everyday routine, because the Mabul was meant to be a rain of Torah, and Noach's teivah, like a sukkah, is the Torah and tefillah that protect a Jew from the flood of the world.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the times of writing and sealing: tzaddikim are written on Rosh Hashanah, others wait for Yom Kippur, later ones for Hoshana Rabbah and Shemini Atzeres, and the Ba'al Shem Tov's disciples revealed a last sealing on Zos Chanukah, for the weaker generations. He finds these periods hinted in the pesukim of Nitzavim, Vayelech and Haazinu. Parshas Noach starts the routine after Tishrei, a new beginning like Noach's new world. He brings that Noach was Moshe's soul, that the Mabul was meant to bring the Torah, and, with the Pri Tzaddik, that it came down as an empty envelope of rain without its inner Torah. At Matan Torah the same flood returned full. Teshuvah precedes Torah, which is why the Mabul began as rains of blessing. Noach's teivah, like a sukkah and a mikveh, is built of holy names and halachos and drew teshuvah into the world; the Ba'al Shem Tov's 'tzohar' is the lit word of Torah and tefillah that saves from today's flood. He closes on the year's closeness to Moshiach and a warning against machlokes.

en: Beyond Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Shemini Atzeres there is a last sealing on Zos Chanukah, for later generations who were not finished with their teshuvah.
The Mabul was meant to bring the Torah down to the world, but since the generation was not worthy, only the outer envelope came down: water without its inner Torah.
At Matan Torah the same flood came down again, this time filled with Torah, which is why the nations thought a new Mabul was coming.
Parshas Noach begins the time of receiving the Torah in a plain, everyday routine, after the special days of Tishrei.

Noach's teivah, like a sukkah and a mikveh, is made of holy names and halachos, and the Ba'al Shem Tov teaches that the teivah is the word of Torah and tefillah, which protects from the flood of the times.
The Mashgiach says this year is a time when Moshiach can come, and one must daven that it not be spoiled, and must stay out of machlokes between tzaddikim.

candidateTopics: zos chanukah as the final sealing

title.en: The last sealing on Zos Chanukah

summary.en: The Mashgiach lists the times of writing and sealing, from Rosh Hashanah through Shemini Atzeres, and brings the tradition from the Ba'al Shem Tov's disciples of a final sealing on Zos Chanukah. He asks why the Gemara does not mention it and answers that later, weaker generations needed it, so it was revealed only then.

title.en: The periods hinted in Nitzavim, Vayelech and Haazinu

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that the 40 pesukim of Nitzavim match the forty days from Rosh Chodesh Elul to Yom Kippur, Vayelech's 30 the thirty days to Rosh Hashanah for complete tzaddikim, Haazinu's 52 the days to Shemini Atzeres, and all 122 together the days until Zos Chanukah.

title.en: Parshas Noach: back to routine, a new world

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the disappointment after Tishrei: a person was created anew on Rosh Hashanah and already spoiled things, like the world destroyed in Noach. He explains that each Shabbos is made of its sedra, like a heavenly kitchen, and that Noach, who came out of the teivah to a new world, teaches to start again from the beginning.

title.en: Noach was Moshe; the Mabul and Matan Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chazal that at Matan Torah the nations ran to Bilaam fearing a new Mabul, and the Gemara in Chullin that 'beshagam' equals Moshe, meaning Moshe's soul was in Noach and the Torah was meant to be given then. Noach did not daven for his generation, so the flood is called 'mei Noach'; Moshe fixed this with 'mecheini na'.

title.en: Shemini Atzeres, geshem and its inner Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Shemini Atzeres is the center point around which the whole 'chag' circle of the year turns, and asks why on such a day we daven for rain. With a mashal of a banana seen by a child and by a doctor, he explains that every physical thing has an inner life, and the inner life of geshem is Torah, which is why Simchas Torah follows the prayer for rain.

title.en: The Mabul as an empty envelope; Matan Torah full

summary.en: Bringing the Pri Tzaddik, the Mashgiach explains that the Mabul was water without its Torah, an empty envelope, while at Matan Torah the same flood returned full of Torah. He retells the Gemara of the nations who saw the same signs as at the Mabul and ran to Bilaam, who answered 'Hashem oz le'amo yiten', and explains with the Gemara and the Maharal why the Torah is bound with the number three.

title.en: Teshuvah before Torah: gishmei brachah

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows parallels between the Mabul and Matan Torah, and explains that Parshas Noach, around Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan, opens the routine of receiving the Torah. With Rashi he explains that the Mabul began as rains of blessing in which Noach saw Torah, and that a flow of teshuvah always comes before Torah, as before Matan Torah and before Moshiach.

title.en: Teivah, sukkah and mikveh: built of holy names

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Hashem had Noach build a teivah for 120 years instead of preaching teshuvah, and explains that, like a sukkah and a mikveh, the teivah is a vessel of holy names built through its halachos. By building it Noach drew teshuvah, which comes from Binah, into the world.

title.en: The 'people of the sukkah' and leaving the teivah

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the Spinka Rebbe's story of chassidim who would not leave the sukkah and were carried off by angels. He applies it to the teivah: Noach built it with its halachos, Moshe passed through a flood twice, and Noach's family and the animals felt such holiness in the teivah that they did not want to leave, until Hashem told them it was now a time of avodah.

title.en: The lit word: a teivah against today's flood

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'tzohar ta'aseh lateivah': put light into every word of Torah and tefillah, which are the teivah that saves from the flood of kefirah and lust of the generation before Moshiach. He adds that the world's autumn, the month of 'Bul', is the spring of Klal Yisroel with Avraham Avinu, and calls for a resolution on Parshas Noach.

title.en: A year close to Moshiach; 5708 was spoiled

summary.en: The Mashgiach says this year, after a shemittah year, is a time fit for Moshiach, but such times were spoiled before. He recounts hearing that Moshiach would come in 5708, and says the state founded then was the opposite of geulah, since by the Rambam Moshiach brings all of Klal Yisroel to keep the Torah; one must daven not to spoil this year.

title.en: Stay out of machlokes between tzaddikim

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the tradition from the Chasam Sofer that the time of the Pnei Yehoshua was fit for Moshiach but was lost in the machlokes between Rabbi Yaakov Emden and Rabbi Yehonasan Eybeschutz. He warns not to take part in machlokes between tzaddikim, tells the story of the rebbetzin of Rabbi Shlomo Leib of Lentshno, and closes with a brachah.

catalogTitle: Important Lessons that are Derived from מעשי אבות, Awareness of קדושת התורה , and the Significance of Learning חומש and רש”י

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches that Torah lifts the one who learns it above time and space, so that learning the Sedros of Bereishis with kedushah means living together with the Avos, and he shows from the Torah's silence about Avraham's merits that the Jewish people exist because creation demanded them.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Midrash that Rebbi cursed Nebuchadnezzar when darshening the Megillah but not when darshening Yirmiyahu, and asks why, since Nebuchadnezzar had been dead for centuries. He answers that Torah is a Toras chaim above time and space, like the Aron that took up no space; one who learns lives in that era. From the Derech Hashem he explains that Hashem reduced the Torah so we can grasp it, and that every halachah, like matzah and bread, holds holy names in a capsule that works even unseen, provided one learns with love, fear and simcha; otherwise it is an empty capsule, as in his story of a man in a library. Turning to Lech Lecha, he urges learning Chumash and Rashi to live with the Avos and awaken inherited emunah. He asks why the Torah never says Avraham was a tzaddik, answers with the Maharal on Moshe's parents, and adds the Ramban on Avraham's faults.

en: Torah is above time and space, so one who learns a passage lives in the era it describes, which is why Rebbi would not curse Nebuchadnezzar while learning Yirmiyahu.
Hashem reduced the Torah through tzimtzum, like a transformer stepping down voltage, so that human senses can grasp it.
Every word of Torah, even learned only by its plain meaning, is a capsule that carries kedushah and nourishes the learner even without his understanding how.
The Derech Hashem sets prerequisites, love and fear of Hashem and honor of the Torah; without them the learning is an empty capsule.
Learning the Sedros of Bereishis properly means accompanying the Avos and awakening the emunah inherited from Avraham Avinu.
Avraham Avinu was not chosen because of his merits; the very purpose of creation compelled a nucleus for the Jewish nation.
The Ramban opens the Sedra with Avraham's two faults to bring out exactly this point.

title.en: Rebbi and the curse of Nebuchadnezzar

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the Tannaim learned by darshening pesukim and tells how the Yetev Lev told a melamed to begin with the source. He brings the Midrash that Rebbi cursed Nebuchadnezzar while darshening the Megillah but not in Yirmiyahu, because one may not curse a king, and asks why, since in Rebbi's day Nebuchadnezzar was long dead.

title.en: Torah above time and space

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that Torah is a Toras chaim above the limits of this world, as the Aron in the Kodesh HaKodashim took up no space. When Rebbi learned Yirmiyahu he lived in that era, when Nebuchadnezzar was a living king; one who learns with kedushah is in heaven while on earth.

title.en: Derech Hashem: the Torah reduced for us

summary.en: The Mashgiach introduces the Ramchal, known for Mesillas Yesharim but also a great mekubal, and brings his Derech Hashem that Torah envelops the learner. Hashem reduced the Torah through tzimtzum so we can grasp it, like a transformer that lowers the voltage for an appliance.

title.en: Holy names in matzah and bread

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that matzah and chametz are the same flour and water, yet the halachos make them different because holy names are within them. Lechem equals three times the Shem Havayah, Torah always comes in threes, salt adds the same again, and matzah equals three times the Shem Havayah in its milui; so every halachah holds holy names reduced into physical things.

title.en: The capsule and its prerequisites

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares Torah to an antibiotic capsule that heals though the patient does not know how; Torah learned by plain pshat still nourishes. The Derech Hashem sets prerequisites, love and fear of Hashem and honor of the Torah, and the Mashgiach describes thinking before learning that one is about to become a Beis HaMikdash, in contrast to learning to outdo another.

title.en: The empty capsule in the library

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a man he once saw studying a Gemara in the Judaica room of the 42nd Street library, whose learning was an empty capsule without kedushah, and adds the image of learning with coffee and a cigar. He speaks of the sweetness of Torah that tzaddikim feel, and brings the end of the Derech Hashem that even an empty capsule keeps a residue that can bring a person back.

title.en: Living with the Avos through the Sedros

summary.en: Turning to Lech Lecha, the Mashgiach says the Sedros must be learned not as history but by living with Avraham Avinu as his guest, as Rebbi lived with Yirmiyahu. Sefer Bereishis is too sublime to be reduced to halachos; its objects are the Avos. He brings the Chasam Sofer that complete emunah needs Chumash and Rashi, explains that inherited emunah lies dormant until the Sedros awaken it, and cites the obligation of shnayim mikra with Rashi.

title.en: Avraham's search and the big question

summary.en: The Mashgiach retells how Avraham, a man of truth, rejected the idols, preached one Creator, was thrown by Nimrod into the fire of Ur Kasdim and survived, and how Hashem then revealed Himself. He then asks why the Torah introduces Noach as a tzaddik but gives no reason for Hashem's favor to Avraham.

title.en: Why Moshe's parents go unnamed

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks the same of Moshe Rabbeinu, whose parents are named only in Va'eira. He brings the Maharal that the world was created for Avraham and the Jewish people, so a Moshe Rabbeinu had to come regardless of who his parents were. In the same way Avraham was the needed nucleus of the nation, a creation rather than a reward, even though he was in truth a greater tzaddik than Noach.

title.en: The Ramban on Avraham's faults; learn the Sedros

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ramban that Avraham erred in endangering Sarah and in leaving Eretz Yisrael in the famine, notes that the Zohar asks and answers these and that the Ramban drew from the Zohar, and explains that the Ramban opens with the faults to show Avraham was not chosen for his righteousness. He mentions the ten tests and closes urging Chumash and Rashi with iyun, citing Rebbe Reb Bunim, as vitamins of emunah and bitachon.

catalogTitle: ביאור על המדרש וגם את נח באהבה זכרת - זה אברהם

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why Noach was saved only 'with love' for the sake of Avraham, because the condition of his entry into the ark was broken in the ark itself, and he applies the ark, the sukkah and the Torah as the refuge of the Jewish people in a time of war and fear.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Midrash that Noach found favor because Avraham would descend from him, and asks why Zichronos says Noach was remembered 'with love' when his rescue was already promised. He explains that the ark was meant to restart creation as before Adam's sin, with Noach's animals as extensions of his own soul, so the lion needed no meat. When Cham sinned in the ark the damage spread, the lion turned predator and maimed Noach, and Noach's wine showed he thought the new world had come. Since the condition was broken, Noach left the ark only in Avraham's merit. The Mashgiach then links the flood to Matan Torah: the flood was water without Torah, and Torah came down as a 'mabul with a shin'. The ark, the sukkah, the mikveh and the Torah are each a refuge outside this world. He applies this to the war of that year, to Gog uMagog and to emunah in hidden times.

en: Noach was saved 'with love' for the sake of Avraham, because the condition on which he entered the ark had been broken and he no longer deserved to be brought out of it.
The ark was meant to restart the world as it was before Adam's sin, and its animals were extensions of Noach's soul, so the lion in it needed no meat.
Cham's sin in the ark spread a flaw to all the creatures linked to Noach, so the lion became a predator and maimed Noach himself.
The flood was meant to be an outpouring of Torah; because the generation was unworthy it came down as empty water, and at Matan Torah the same flood came down as Torah.
The ark, the sukkah, the mikveh and the Torah are each a place outside this world where judgment cannot reach, and after Sukkos the Torah becomes the Jew's refuge.
The Mashgiach says Jews in a time of war must know that Hashem runs every war, and that this emunah and bitachon is itself the sukkah that protects them.

torah as ark, sukkah and mikveh

title.en: Noach remembered 'with love' for Avraham

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Noach found favor because Avraham would come from him, against the passuk that calls Noach a tzaddik. He asks why Zichronos opens with Noach being remembered 'with love', when Hashem had already promised before the flood that Noach would enter the ark and come out to keep life on earth.

title.en: Why the lion maimed Noach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi that Noach was late feeding the lion, which injured him and left him blemished. He asks why Hashem, who helped Noach feed every creature on time, did not help him with the lion, and discusses the Ibn Ezra and Rashi on what food, including meat, Noach brought into the ark.

title.en: How man's sins corrupt creation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem made a harmonious world like Gan Eden, and man builds or destroys it with his deeds. The sins of the generation of the flood corrupted even the animals and the ground, and he brings the Ramban that before Adam's sin no beast was predatory, as will again be in the days of Moshiach.

title.en: The ark as a new beginning

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem decided to wipe out the corrupted world and begin again with Noach and the animals that had not sinned. A person's possessions are an extension of his soul, as Reb Tzadok HaKohen explains about the donkey of Rebbi Pinchas ben Yair, so the animals in the ark were Noach's sparks and stayed pure, and the lion in the ark needed no meat.

title.en: Cham's sin spreads to the lion

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Cham sinned in the ark. Since Cham was part of Noach's family, the flaw spread to all the creatures linked to Noach: the lion became a predator that straw could not satisfy, and when Noach was late it maimed him. He adds the Zohar that outer blemishes reflect the soul and Rashi on Korach that a sin can reach one's forebears.

title.en: Noach's wine and the broken condition

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Noach planted a vineyard and drank because he thought the renewed world, when one may drink a great cup as in the days of Moshiach and Eliyahu, had already come. But Cham's sin had annulled the condition of the ark, so Hashem was not bound to bring Noach out; He did so only in mercy, for the sake of Avraham, and that is why the verse appears in Zichronos.

title.en: Chizuk after the Yamim Noraim; rains of blessing

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Parshas Noach is a chizuk for a Jew who feels he has lost what he gained over Tishrei: he is still of Avraham's seed and will in the end be good. He then brings Rashi that the flood began as rains of blessing in case they repented, and explains that even after Yom Kippur's sealing, teshuvah could have turned the decree around.

title.en: Noach, Moshe and the Torah meant for the flood generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that at Matan Torah the nations ran to Bilaam fearing a new flood, and the Zera Kodesh that Noach was reborn as Moshe: the Torah was meant for the generation of the flood, but Noach did not daven enough, and as Moshe he gave himself for Klal Yisrael. He explains with the Zohar and the Chasam Sofer that the rain of Shemini Atzeres carries Torah, so the flood was empty water without Torah.

title.en: A flood of Torah: the mabul with a shin

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the nations saw the same alignment of stars as at the flood, and Bilaam answered that a flood was indeed coming down, but of Torah. With the Maharal on the Torah's connection to three he explains the letter shin, and reads 'bashalom' as 'mabul' with a shin. He links the opened heavens of the flood and of Matan Torah, the forty days of each, and Moshe saved from the water in an ark.

title.en: Yaakov flees to Sukkos; the sukkah as refuge

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zera Kodesh that Yaakov's gifts to Esav were a se'ir la'azazel, as Yom Kippur appeases the Satan, and that afterwards Yaakov fled to Sukkos, as Jews flee into the sukkah. The sukkah is a piece of heaven in this world, like an embassy, where judgment cannot reach, and therefore it needs exact halachos, because its holy names come through the halachah.

title.en: The ark, the Torah and the mikveh

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the ark, like the sukkah, separated Noach from this world, and therefore it too was given exact measurements. He brings the Imrei Emes that after Sukkos the Torah becomes the Jew's sukkah and city of refuge, and explains that the mikveh is also outside this world, where one is reborn, and that the Torah is compared to a mikveh.

title.en: The word of Torah and tefillah as today's ark

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ba'al Shem Tov that the teivah of 'tzohar ta'aseh lateivah' is the word of tefillah and Torah, which must shine with one's whole heart, as he heard from his rebbe, Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz. Today's world is a flood of heresy and immorality, and the Torah is the ark, sukkah and mikveh that saves; in Cheshvan, when a flood comes each year, Jews hold on to the Torah.

title.en: The war, Gog uMagog and Hashem's kindness

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the war that began on the night of Hoshana Rabbah and the fear of Gog uMagog, and points to Hashem's kindness in a Sukkos when the rain stopped exactly when it was needed. From Chizkiyahu and the Exodus he shows that Gog uMagog need not bring suffering and that Hashem can change decrees, and he says Hashem pleads with Jews to flee into the ark, the sukkah and the Torah, as a small group protects all of Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Bar Daroma, Ben Koziva and reliance on strength

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the Gemara of Bar Daroma, the warrior who struck down Romans until he said 'Have You not abandoned us' and died, and suggests he is the Ben Koziva of the Yerushalmi whom Rebbi Akiva thought was Moshiach. Drawing on the Rambam and the Chasam Sofer, he explains that he could have been Moshiach but failed because the people relied on his strength, and that the snake that killed him is the force that makes Jews forget that Hashem runs the world.

title.en: The origin of Vehu Rachum

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the story brought in the Kol Bo of a ship of Jews fleeing Yerushalayim whose king demanded they enter a fire. After thirty days of fasting, a simple Jew dreamed of a passuk with two 'ki' and three 'lo', a sage identified it in Yeshayahu, the man entered the fire unharmed, and three tzaddikim appeared and composed the long Vehu Rachum. The Mashgiach connects the passuk to the haftarah just read.

title.en: Decrees turned to the nations; emunah in hiddenness

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that the decrees of Gog uMagog can be turned onto the nations, as a kaparah, from the haftarah's 'I have given Egypt as your ransom'. He says the prophecy is for every generation, that ours is like the tribe of Dan who were last and outside the clouds yet enter them with the power of sukkah and Torah, and that Jews must strengthen their emunah that everything in the news is hashgachah pratis, finding Hashem in a time of hester like Megillas Esther. The recording breaks off.

catalogTitle: נח רצה לעשות עולם התיקון. אלא שחסר לו תפילה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Noach was meant to rebuild the world as a rectified world, tried to repair its ruin through the raven and the vineyard, and failed because he had Torah but lacked tefillah, and from there he speaks at length about prayer as the ark of our own generation.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach asks why Noach, whose rescue was planned from the start, needed the special remembrance of Rosh Hashanah, why the lion bit him, and why the raven failed its mission. He explains that Hashem wanted the ark to bring out a rectified world like the one before Adam's sin, but Cham, the raven and the dog sinned in the ark and ruined the plan. Through Eliyahu, the angel of the covenant, he shows what that world looks like: wine can be drunk, the raven feeds others, the lion eats straw. Noach tried to repair the damage, first by sending the raven, then by planting a vineyard to drink Eliyahu's cup, but became drunk. He had Torah but lacked tefillah. The Mashgiach then teaches about prayer at length: the Ba'al Shem Tov's 'light in the teivah', kavanah, emunah and closeness, stories of tzaddikim, and tefillah as the ark in today's flood.

en: Hashem planned that Noach would come out of the ark into a rectified world like the one before Adam's sin, but the sin of Cham, the raven and the dog in the ark ruined that plan.
Noach could not repair the damage because he had Torah but lacked tefillah, and only tefillah can annul a decree and bring a salvation.
Tefillah is 'service of the heart': it must be said slowly, with understanding, devotion and a warm heart, not rushed through.
Praying for one's needs is itself an act of emunah and of cleaving to Hashem, and its highest level is to delight in the closeness until one forgets what one came to ask.
One must ask Hashem for every small thing, since there is no one else to ask.
Tefillah faces the strongest yetzer hara and is mocked, yet in the generation before Moshiach it is the main service.
Today's world is a flood, and the word of tefillah is the ark that protects a Jew and carries him to the shore of the geulah.

candidateTopics: prayer in the generation before Moshiach

title.en: Remembering Noach, and two puzzles from the ark

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Maggid of Mezritch on the holiness that rests on ten Jews gathered together, then asks what was so great in 'Vayizkor Elokim es Noach' of the Rosh Hashanah Zichronos if Noach's rescue was planned from the start. He raises two questions: why Noach lacked the heavenly help to feed the lion on time, so that it bit him, and why the raven did not carry out its mission, and why Noach sent the raven at all.

title.en: The plan of a rectified world and its ruin in the ark

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that after the flood Hashem wanted to begin again with a rectified world like the one before Adam's sin, and Noach entered the ark for that. But Cham, the raven and the dog sinned in the ark, and the plan was undone; by the Midrash, Noach found favor only because Avraham would descend from him, and this is the remembrance of 'Vayizkor'.

title.en: Eliyahu, angel of the covenant, and the cup of wine

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Eliyahu, who is Pinchas, embodies the holiness of the covenant, and that Noach is called tzaddik for the same holiness, like Yosef. Through the Gemara in Berachos on wine and Dovid's great cup in the future, he shows that wine is dangerous until the rectified world comes with Eliyahu, which is why Eliyahu's cup on Pesach night remains undrunk.

title.en: The cruel raven and the lion that ate straw

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Eliyahu belongs to the rectified world, and through him even the raven, the cruelest of birds, is repaired and feeds a stranger. In the rectified world the lion will eat straw; in the ark it did, but after the sin it needed meat that was not there, Noach lost his heavenly help, and the lion bit him.

title.en: Noach's two attempts at repair: the raven and the vineyard

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Noach sent the raven, one of the sinners, on a mitzvah mission on Shabbos to repair it, but it could not receive holiness; its repair waits for Eliyahu. Then Noach planted a vineyard to make kiddush and drink Eliyahu's cup, but became drunk, and 'vayishkar' equals 'kos shel Eliyahu Hanavi' in gematria.

title.en: Torah alone cannot annul a decree

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Noach, a tzaddik who learned Torah, could not complete the repair, and answers that he lacked tefillah. He brings, from Reb Yechezkel Levenstein's sefer, the Midrash that in Haman's time Moshe told Eliyahu that only Mordechai's prayer could annul the decree, and he describes the troubles surrounding Jews today.

title.en: 'Tzohar ta'aseh lateivah': light in the word of prayer

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's reading of 'make a light for the teivah' as bringing light into each word of prayer, and says one must not rush davening. The hint is given to Noach because he did not pray for his generation, so the flood is called 'mei Noach'; Moshe, his gilgul, repaired this with 'mecheini na'. Tefillah is service of the heart in place of the korbanos.

title.en: Kavanah in the first berachah

summary.en: The Mashgiach discusses the words of tefillah and its kavanah, how the Rabbanan set the first berachah of Avos as the place for kavanah, Tosafos on their power, and why the poskim say that one who lacked kavanah there today does not repeat, since our small generations are 'drunk, but not from wine'.

title.en: Tefillah as emunah and closeness to Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that praying for parnassah is not a lowly request but emunah, the first of the Ten Commandments, and that tefillah means cleaving to Hashem, the aim of all the mitzvos. He brings the Sfas Emes on Chana, who was content after praying before knowing the answer, and says the true level is to delight in standing before the King who bends His ear to a Jew's prayer.

title.en: Emunah in hiding, and asking for every small thing

summary.en: Through 'vetzaddik be'emunaso yichyeh' the Mashgiach says that in late, weak generations the main thing is emunah, and a Jew's prayer in a dark world of hester panim makes his emunah shine more than in earlier generations. He tells of the Rebbe of Chernobyl, who prayed about the maid leaving, and Reb Dovid'l of Talne, who before the shofar realized that even a roll must be asked of Hashem.

title.en: The worm and the wind: hashgachah and nearness

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the Ba'al Shem Tov's story of a wind sent across a whole region to save one worm from the sun, and draws that a Jew, small as he is, is watched over by Hashem. Facing Yerushalayim in prayer, by the Ba'al Shem Tov's teaching that a person is where his thoughts are and the Gemara's case of the traveler who fixes his Shabbos place by a distant tree, places him in the Beis Hamikdash, near Hashem.

title.en: Tzafra veramsha: a Jew may sing at any hour

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Hashem is the center of every heartbeat and breath, and brings 'kamah lecha besari' as a closeness without parallel. Every creature sings to Hashem only at its appointed time, birds in the morning and insects at night, but a Jew sings 'tzafra veramsha' and can pour out his heart at any moment; that closeness is a delight no worldly pleasure can match.

title.en: The Yaaros Devash's portion, and preparing for davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Kuzari that tefillah is the heart and fruit of the day, and the letter of the Yaaros Devash, the great Rabbi Yonasan Eibeschutz, who says that despite being laughed at for his long Shemoneh Esrei, his portion from all his toil is standing before Hashem in prayer. He adds that one must prepare and come early, from the Magen Avraham, the Tanya and the Rokeach, who compares the words of prayer to counting money.

title.en: Why prayer meets the greatest opposition

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of the Beis Aharon, who answered a chassid's tale of a poretz sledding over a field of sugar by asking how that compares to the pleasure of Nishmas. He brings that the greater a mitzvah, the greater its yetzer hara, and the Gemara that prayer 'stands at the height of the world' yet people belittle it; before Moshiach prayer is the main thing, and he adds Reb Yisrael Salanter and the Chasam Sofer, who as a bachur davened long and lost no learning.

title.en: Tefillah as the ark in today's flood

summary.en: Returning to the Ba'al Shem Tov, the Mashgiach adds 'come into the teivah' with all one's strength, and brings Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz: today's world, with its new technology, is a stormy flood, and the word of prayer is the ark that shelters a Jew until the shore of the geulah. He urges choosing a shul of serious daveners, learning the meaning of the words, and brings that each word of prayer is a palace guarded by angels.

title.en: The free taste, the king's daughter, and a closing tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's mashal of the grocer who gives one grape to taste and then asks for payment: Hashem sometimes gives a sweet prayer as a gift and then expects work. From the Zohar's mashal of the king's daughter promised to whoever kills the snake, he explains that one wins tefillah by overcoming the yetzer hara and guarding the holiness of the covenant and of speech, and he closes with accepting love of every Jew before davening and a tefillah for the geulah.

catalogTitle: ישמעאל's Occupation of ארץ ישראל In our times

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains the debate between Yitzchak and Yishmael behind the Akedah: Klal Yisrael exists by miracle and is bound to Hashem by a love beyond reason, while Yishmael, the 'pere adam' fighting the Jews today, gives his life only for his own desires.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Rashi on the Akedah: Yishmael boasted that he was circumcised at thirteen, and Yitzchak answered that he would give all his limbs to Hashem. This debate, he says, is the seed of today's war between Yishmael and the Jews, and its outcome will bring Moshiach ben David from Yitzchak. Since Yitzchak's birth was a miracle, the very existence of Klal Yisrael is a miracle, seen in a small Eretz Yisrael surrounded by the Arabs, the 'pere adam' who follow no logic. He distinguishes love based on benefit from essential love, the love of a father for a son, and says this bond is why even sinners gave their lives rather than convert, as in the story of the Shpoler Zeide's two thieves. The Akedah was the greatest test because it shattered Avraham's life ambition, unlike martyrdom for an ideal or, as with the suicide bombers, for lust. Milah at eight days and the Akedah both show a bond above reason, which is why Jews recall the Akedah when asking for mercy.

en: The debate between Yitzchak and Yishmael before the Akedah is the root of today's war between Yishmael and the Jews, which will end with Yishmael's fall and Moshiach ben David from Yitzchak.
Because Yitzchak was born by a miracle, the essence and the continued existence of Klal Yisrael are a miracle, while Yishmael was born naturally.
The bond between Hashem and a Jew is an essential love, like a father's love for his son, which does not depend on behavior or benefit.
The Akedah was the greatest test because it meant destroying the very ambition for which Avraham had been willing to die, without any reason except his bond to Hashem.
Milah at eight days, without understanding, and the Akedah express the same thing: a Jew's bond to Hashem is above reason.
Yishmael's self-sacrifice, as with the suicide bombers, is for his own pleasure, while a Jew's self-sacrifice comes from his bond to Hashem.

candidateTopics: existence of Klal Yisrael as a miracle
essential love between Hashem and Klal Yisrael
Arab terror and the war in Eretz Yisrael

title.en: The debate before the Akedah

summary.en: The Mashgiach chooses to speak about the Akedah from a new angle and brings Rashi on 'after these things': Yishmael boasted that he was circumcised at thirteen by choice, and Yitzchak answered that he would give all his limbs to Hashem, which the Akedah then proved.

title.en: Today's war between Yitzchak and Yishmael

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the present conflict is the war between Yitzchak and Yishmael, bringing the Baal HaTurim that when Yishmael falls Moshiach ben David from Yitzchak will come. To understand its root he looks to the first seed of the dispute in this week's parsha, since the essence of a thing is seen at its beginning.

title.en: Klal Yisrael exists by a miracle; Yishmael the 'pere adam'

summary.en: Yishmael was born naturally, while Yitzchak's birth to aged parents was a miracle, so Klal Yisrael's existence is a miracle, as Rabbi Yaakov Emden writes and as its survival of all the empires shows. A small Eretz Yisrael surrounded by Arabs is a miracle, since Yishmael is a 'pere adam', wild in essence and only human in appearance.

title.en: Why the Arabs do not overrun the Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chofetz Chaim's words that a Yishmaelite stays a 'pere adam' whatever profession he takes, and points to the attack on the Twin Towers. He asks why such people, who ignore world opinion, do not attack the Jews of Eretz Yisrael, and answers that it is a miracle: Klal Yisrael has lived supernaturally since Avraham and Sarah.

title.en: Love of benefit and essential love

summary.en: The Mashgiach distinguishes a love based on benefit, which is really self-love, from essential love like a father's for his son, and says the love between Hashem and Klal Yisrael is greater still and does not depend on behavior, as the navi says 'I love you'. This is why even sinners in the times of the Crusades gave their lives rather than convert.

title.en: The Shpoler Zeide and the two thieves

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Shpoler Zeide, who disliked noisy davening, explained what true hand-clapping is: two former students of his who became thieves were caught stealing from a church and, set on fire, refused to convert and clapped their hands declaring their belief in Hashem.

title.en: Why the Akedah was the greatest test

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Hashem said that failing the Akedah would void the earlier tests, and why it was harder than Avraham's being thrown into Nimrod's fire before he was a navi. He then describes kinds of self-sacrifice among people: for fame, for a king, for a team or party.

title.en: What drives the suicide bombers

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Arab suicide bombers give their lives for lust: he brings Rashi that the sons of Yishmael refused the Torah because of 'do not commit adultery', and the Gemara that nine of ten measures of immorality went to the Arabs. They are promised such pleasure in the afterlife, and they give their lives for it.

title.en: Avraham's life ambition

summary.en: Avraham's ambition, for which he gave his life in the fire, was to make Hashem known in the world. Hashem promised him Yitzchak, from whom the Jewish nation would spread the knowledge of one G-d, and the Mashgiach notes that the other religions took the idea of one G-d and of Moshiach from the Jews.

title.en: The Akedah shatters Avraham's ambition

summary.en: Commanding him to slaughter Yitzchak meant destroying the nation that was to spread Hashem's name. Though Hashem only asked and did not command, Avraham did not argue, because he was bound to Hashem with an essential love; this self-sacrifice without reason, unlike his earlier one for an ideal, is found only among Jews.

title.en: Milah, the Akedah and today's Yishmael

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to the debate: Milah is done at eight days because it is above reason, and Yitzchak proved at the Akedah, going with joy, that a Jew is bound to Hashem beyond logic. He contrasts Yishmael's self-sacrifice for pleasure with Jewish martyrs, even simple people at the Spanish expulsion, and explains that Jews recall the Bris and the Akedah when asking for mercy.

catalogTitle: הנקודה של מגן אברהם אינו נפגם לעולם

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Jew carries a point of Avraham Avinu, above free choice and never damaged, which the melave malka of David HaMelech strengthens and which alone protects a Jew from being swallowed by the 'kiss' of the present exile of Edom.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the melave malka as the meal of David HaMelech: the luz bone, which did not benefit from Adam's sin, is nourished only by this meal, and from it comes techiyas hameisim. He then describes Sefer Bereishis as the creation of the point of Klal Yisrael in the Avos, so that every Jew holds a piece of Avraham, guarded by 'Magen Avraham' and never damaged. Following the Maharal, Avraham's choosing has no stated reason, since he was the purpose of creation; this point is above free choice, which is why the parsha ends with milah at eight days. Melave malka, Shabbos and Kiddush Levanah all express this lasting point. Turning to the four kings, he identifies Tidal, 'king of nations', with Edom, whose weapon is the kiss of closeness, and brings Yaakov's instruction in Egypt to declare openly that Jews only sojourn there. Contact with the point of Avraham is the compass in exile.

en: Every Jew has within him a point of Avraham Avinu, guarded by 'Magen Avraham', which can never be damaged.
This point is above free choice, which is why milah is given at eight days without asking the child.
The melave malka is the meal of David HaMelech, which nourishes the luz bone and is bound up with techiyas hameisim.
At melave malka one is meant to strengthen one's emunah and know that one's point can never be extinguished.
The exile of Edom, 'Tidal king of nations', attacks Jews mainly through the kiss of closeness and joining, not only through the bite.
The only protection in exile is to declare openly that one does not belong among the nations, as Yaakov instructed his sons in Egypt.

title.en: Melave malka, the meal of David HaMelech

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares David's midnight prayer, which remained for chassidim, with the fourth Shabbos meal, the melave malka, and asks what it has to do with David. He answers that the luz bone, which did not benefit from Adam's sin, is nourished only by this meal and is the root of techiyas hameisim, and David, the tikkun of Adam, is 'chai vekayam'.

title.en: Bereishis as the creation of Klal Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Sefer Bereishis is a book of creation also in the sense that it records the creation of the point of Klal Yisrael in Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, while Sefer Shemos tells of its spreading into the twelve tribes. Every Jew holds a piece of Avraham, which is why the first berachah of Shemoneh Esrei ends with 'Magen Avraham'.

title.en: The point of Avraham awakens each year

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the stories of the Avos are not history: reading the parsha awakens the point of Avraham in every Jew, like strings that resonate together. 'Magen Avraham' guards that point so it can never be damaged, and from it comes 'mechayeh meisim'. He adds that the world was created for Avraham, as Chazal read 'behibaram' as 'b'Avraham'.

title.en: Avraham chosen without a reason; milah above choice

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Maharal's question why the Torah explains Noach's merit but gives no reason for Avraham's choosing, and answers that Avraham was the purpose of creation and his choosing comes from the Divine will alone. From this he explains why the parsha ends with milah at eight days: the point of Avraham is in every Jew without his choice, above nature, like the eight-stringed harp of Moshiach, and the Shabbos meals feed this emunah.

title.en: Techiyas hameisim, Shabbos and the maftir

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that only Jews will rise at techiyas hameisim, because they have a point that can never be lost; at melave malka one strengthens this emunah, as in Kiddush Levanah where the moon always renews. Shabbos, fixed by Hashem's will and not by beis din, is like this point; the maftir, an eighth reading that repeats what was read, belongs to David and Moshiach, whose spark accompanies a Jew into the dark weekdays.

title.en: What covers the point; the four kings

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that many Jews have lost contact with their point and asks what covers it; he identifies the covering as the 'se'or', the yetzer hara, the klipah of Amalek and Edom. He then turns to the four kings in the parsha and to the Midrash about the name Tidal, asking why only Tidal's name is preceded by a vav.

title.en: Tidal, Edom and the kiss of Eisav

summary.en: Following the Ramban, the Mashgiach identifies the four kings with the four exiles and Tidal 'king of nations' with Edom, an exile that passes from nation to nation. He brings Eisav's kiss, which was really a bite, and explains that Edom's tactic is closeness and dialogue; the vav before Tidal shows that connecting is his essence, and one must flee his kiss.

title.en: Emancipation, Napoleon, and 'vayagar sham'

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the breaking of the ghetto walls and equal rights as the danger of joining the nations, and tells of the dispute among tzaddikim over Napoleon, where the Ba'al HaTanya feared the freedom it would bring. He then explains the Haggadah's 'vayagar sham': Yaakov instructed his sons to tell Pharaoh plainly that they had come only to sojourn, the one protection against drowning in exile.

title.en: The test of false leaders before Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash that before Moshiach the erev rav will set up a kohen gadol of their own, and asks how a Jew will know whom to follow. He answers that one who is in contact with the point of Avraham and David cannot be led astray.

title.en: The point as a compass; Avraham alone

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls the point a compass that shows every Jew his direction, and says that at melave malka Jews carry the light of Shabbos into the weekdays and follow the tzaddikim who make no innovations. He closes with Avraham, who went out alone with Eliezer against the kings, and says that with the strength of his point and of simple emunah a Jew can withstand the exile.

catalogTitle: רבינו בחיי - לך לך' לך אל שורש שלך - ארץ ישראל

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains, following Rabbeinu Bachya, that 'Lech lecha' means going back to one's root, Eretz Yisrael and the Torah, and shows how every step of the parsha is Avraham Avinu cutting away what is not his.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Rabbeinu Bachya: 'Lech lecha' means 'go to yourself', to your root, and the root of every Jew is Eretz Yisrael, bound to the upper land and Olam Haba. A Jew's longing for the land comes from his neshamah, and learning Torah about it is tasting it, not reading a description. Not everyone feels this taste at once; he tells of a talmid of R' Nachum of Chernobyl and compares the land to a diamond. The whole Torah is built around Eretz Yisrael; mitzvos in chutz laaretz are signposts. Following the Ramban, the deeds of the avos are a sign for the children: the going down to Egypt and the four kings foreshadow the exiles and the four kingdoms, which also stand against the four avos nezikin, which have no permanence. The parsha is a program of separation: from Lot, from the money of Sedom, from Yishmael, ending with milah. Each Jew is a part of Avraham and must learn the sedra as his own life.

en: Following Rabbeinu Bachya, 'Lech lecha' means going to one's own root, and the root of every Jew is Eretz Yisrael, bound to Olam Haba.
Every Jew has a natural longing for Eretz Yisrael because his neshamah comes from the same place as the Torah, where the land draws from.
The whole Torah is built around Eretz Yisrael; it opens and closes with the land, and the mitzvos kept in chutz laaretz are signposts pointing back to it.
What happened to Avraham Avinu is a sign for his children: his descent to Egypt and his war with the four kings foreshadow the exiles and the four kingdoms.
The parsha is a program of returning to the root by cutting off what is foreign: Lot, the wealth offered by the king of Sedom, Yishmael, and finally the orlah through milah.
Every Jew was once a part of Avraham Avinu, so the sedra must be learned as Toras chaim about oneself, not as history.

title.en: Lech lecha: go to your root

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rabbeinu Bachya that 'Lech lecha' means go to yourself, to your root, which is Eretz Yisrael, bound to the upper land and Olam Haba. Every Jew longs for the land because of his neshamah, and learning Torah about it is like tasting food rather than reading about it.

title.en: Not everyone feels the taste

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Avraham did not see the land's greatness at once, and that the longing for it is purely spiritual. He compares it to a Jew who feels the kedushah of Shabbos in the kiddush wine, brings R' Aharon of Karlin on the word 'kamah' as a longing, and says some feel no taste in Eretz Yisrael or only a national feeling.

title.en: A land paved with diamonds

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a talmid of R' Nachum of Chernobyl who described Eretz Yisrael as paved with diamonds, and of a Jew who came there and at first saw nothing, until after three months he felt it. He explains that at first the land looks like any other, as a beginner feels no taste in a blatt Gemara, but whoever does not give up is shown it.

title.en: A diamond, and mitzvos as signposts

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Eretz Yisrael is geographically tiny but is like a diamond, where size does not matter. The whole Torah is built around the land, and he brings Rashi that the mitzvos are kept in chutz laaretz so they will not be new when the Jews return.

title.en: The Torah opens and closes with the land

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that the Torah opens and ends with Eretz Yisrael and brings the Ramban that the Torah was given to be kept in the land. He explains 'set up signposts' to mean that the true 'tziyunim' are Jews who keep the Torah in exile, brings the Chesed L'Avraham on the soul of one living in the land, and says we stand at the end of the last exile.

title.en: The deeds of the avos as a sign

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ramban that Avraham's life was a mirror of his children's future, and the Ramban's complaint that going down to Egypt and endangering Sarah caused the Egyptian exile. He asks how the Ramban could say this, answers that something was there because the heavenly plan for golus had to be carried out through the avos, and brings the Midrash that the four kings are the four kingdoms.

title.en: The four avos nezikin

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer quoting R' Menachem Azaria of Fano that the four avos nezikin stand against the four kingdoms and the four letters of Hashem's Name, since everything in the world has its root in the Torah. He adds that when a person is brought to learn Seder Nezikin it is a sign he needs a yeshuah, and the learning is the cure.

title.en: Nezikin have no permanence

summary.en: Returning to R' Menachem Azaria of Fano, the Mashgiach explains why the Mishnah of the shomrim says 'hen' but the avos nezikin cannot carry that word of existence. He then explains why the Mishnah of avos nezikin is 'not upheld': nezikin have no lasting existence, and in the days of Moshiach, as Yeshayahu says, there will be no harm and the yetzer hara will become a longing to learn.

title.en: The parsha of the root; Lot as an attachment

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the root of Klal Yisrael is Torah, Elokus and Eretz Yisrael, and the whole parsha, named Lech Lecha, is about returning to the root by cutting away the bad. Lot was an attachment to Avraham, not his essence; because of Lot Avraham had to go down to Egypt, and on returning he separated from Lot.

title.en: The shepherds' quarrel and the Kenaani

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi that Lot's shepherds grazed on others' land and the Ramban's different reading, and asks why the pasuk mentions the Kenaani and Perizi. He brings Avraham's words to Avimelech that there is no fear of G-d in this place: he felt a drop in yiras Shamayim among sinners, and says the place a person is in affects him, so one should daven among good Jews.

title.en: A riv, not a merivah

summary.en: The Mashgiach first suggests that the Kenaani-Perizi quarrel filled the air with machlokes and caused the shepherds' quarrel, then rejects this. Bad company is the worst influence, so Hashem plants a protective hatred between the tzaddik's followers and the rasha's; that is why the pasuk calls it a 'riv', and Avraham, understanding this, separated from Lot.

title.en: Tidal king of nations: the bite and the kiss

summary.en: After the separation from Lot comes the war of the four kings, the four kelipos. The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Tidal 'king of nations' is Edom, a mixture of all nations, and R' Yochanan's proof. He explains Esav's kiss as a bite in another form and says the last tactic of Edom is friendship and joining, yet Avraham defeated all four kings.

title.en: The money of Sedom and Yishmael

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the king of Sedom wanted to make Avraham rich, and Avraham refused lest it be said 'I made Avram rich'. He compares this to the deep exile of today when mosdos depend on the nations' money, then says the birth of Yishmael was another kelipah Avraham had to separate from himself, and that today Yishmael has become great as the Torah says.

title.en: Milah, and learning the sedra as one's own

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the sedra ends with milah, the last orlah cut away, when Avraham reaches his pure root. Every Jew was part of Avraham and went through his trials, so the sedra is Toras chaim, not history; Avraham was mocked as a madman, and the Mashgiach calls for kavanah in the brachah Magen Avraham.

catalogTitle: המדות טובות של א"א הם ירושה לכלל ישראל

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Avraham Avinu was a new kind of creation, and that every Jew inherits from him not only a soul but a body that carries the good middos of the Avos.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the first bracha of Shemoneh Esrei: tefillah rises through the Avos, and the greatest praise of Hashem is that Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov lived in His world. He urges deep study of their parshiyos, describes Avraham's trials, and brings the Midrash of the burning palace as a model for holding on to emunah in dark times. Through a mashal of a ruined building he shows how Bereishis and Noach were a chain of disappointments until Avraham came as a new species, the purpose of creation. A Jew differs from a gentile in body as well as soul: kindness, shame and mercy are middos of the body, inherited from the Avos, which is why the covenant of milah is in the flesh and why dayanim need yichus. With this he explains Avraham's fear and Eliezer's role, and closes that every Jew is Avraham's heir and should rejoice in that inheritance.

en: The first bracha of Shemoneh Esrei needs special kavanah because tefillos rise through the Avos, and emunah is an inheritance from them.
Bereishis and Noach record one disappointment after another; the world reached its purpose only with Avraham, a new species that believes in Hashem by nature.
A Jew's body is different from a gentile's: mercy, shame and kindness are middos of the body, inherited from Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov.
Hashem's covenant with Noach is in the heavens, while His covenant with Avraham is in the flesh, because a Jew serves Hashem with his body.
Hashem's promise that Avraham's heir would come 'from his innards' means physical children, whose very bodies would be holy.
Every Jew carries a spark of Avraham Avinu and is his heir in body, and the Mashgiach says one should rejoice in this inheritance.
