title.en: Davening through the Avos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the first bracha of Shemoneh Esrei needs special kavanah: tefillos rise through the Avos, and the greatest praise of Hashem is that men like Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov lived in His world. Emunah itself is an inheritance from them, above all from Avraham.

title.en: Learning the parshiyos of the Avos; Avraham's trials

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the parshiyos of the Avos hold the foundations of emunah and must be learned in depth. He describes Avraham's trials, among them a father who handed him over to Nimrod, asks how a father could do this, and answers with the Maharal that Avraham was a new creation with no real bond to Terach.

title.en: Avraham in Mitzrayim; the middos of the Avos

summary.en: From Rashi on 'hinei na yadati' the Mashgiach shows that Avraham's extraordinary guarding of his eyes weakened once he entered the atmosphere of Mitzrayim, and he draws how important it is to choose friends and surroundings. Along the way he explains that the first three brachos correspond to the Avos and that the three middos of the Jewish people come from them.

title.en: The burning palace

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the Midrash of the man who saw a palace burning: Avraham looked at the corrupt world of Nimrod and asked whether it has no owner, until Hashem revealed Himself as the Owner. He applies it to every Jew's dark moments, saying one must hold fast to emunah until the light comes.

title.en: Two 'lech lecha's, Avraham's fear, and Eliezer

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash on the two times Hashem said 'lech lecha' and the Midrash that the world was created for Avraham. He then raises the Ramban's question on 'what will You give me', and the difficulty from the Ramban's own rule that a prophecy accompanied by a symbolic act must be fulfilled, and asks why Eliezer, a student who drew Torah from Avraham, had to lead the yeshiva.

title.en: The mashal of the grand building

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells a mashal of a magnificent new hall whose opening celebration falls apart: the air conditioner fails, the windows stick, water floods in and the roof collapses. He sets it against the creation of the world, which Hashem saw as good and celebrated with Shabbos.

title.en: The disappointments of Bereishis and Noach

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the first two parshiyos as a chain of disappointments: Adam's sin, Kayin's murder of Hevel, the generation of Enosh, Hashem's regret even over Noach, Chanoch taken away early, and after the flood Noach's drunkenness, Nimrod and the generation of the dispersion.

title.en: Avraham, a new creation

summary.en: With 'I will make you a great nation' the Mashgiach explains that Hashem promised a new species, a person who believes in Hashem by instinct. From the pesukim said in davening ('You chose Avram... and found his heart faithful') and the Midrash 'behibaram - be'Avraham' he shows that creation was completed only with Avraham, its purpose.

title.en: The Jewish body is different

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Avraham's new species differs in the soul and also in the body, as the Tanya explains with kelipas nogah. He compares it to Shabbos, which looks the same yet is another world, says the purpose of creation is to refine the body, and shows that the good middos come from the body, so that even a Jew far from Torah keeps his rachmanus.

title.en: Shame, and serving Hashem with the body

summary.en: From the Gemara on why one who admits part of a claim must swear (a man does not brazenly deny to his creditor's face) the Mashgiach shows that a Jew, even a dishonest one, remains a bayshan by inheritance. He adds the Midrash that gentiles can bring only olos while Jews bring shelamim, because a Jew can serve Hashem with his body, even by eating.

title.en: Two covenants: Noach and Avraham

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Hashem's covenant with Noach, the rainbow in the sky that asks mankind to look up and forget the body, with His covenant with Avraham in the flesh, where holiness is to shine in the body. He brings the Kotzker's reading of 'the heavens are Hashem's and the earth He gave to man': man is to make the earth into heaven, and only Jews can do this.

title.en: Yichus for dayanim; children in body and in soul

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why dayanim of capital cases and the Great Sanhedrin need yichus, and suggests that rachmanus passes through the body, just as an old or childless man may not sit on the Sanhedrin. He then distinguishes inheritance in the body from inheritance in the soul, with the exchange between the Ba'al HaTanya and Reb Baruch of Mezhibuzh and the convert who says 'to our fathers' over bikkurim.

title.en: Why Avraham thought Eliezer would inherit

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers the question on the Ramban: the first promise to Avraham's 'seed' could be read as children of the soul, his talmidim, and Eliezer, who drew Torah from him, already was one. He then explains why Eliezer led the yeshiva and court: as long as Avraham had no children he could not judge capital cases, so he appointed Eliezer, and an appointment once made remains, as with a kohen gadol who was replaced.

title.en: Children 'from your innards'

summary.en: Hashem answered that the heir would come from Avraham's innards, the lowest organs, and the Mashgiach connects this to Asher Yatzar, said before the Kisei HaKavod, and to Rashi's 'lifted above the stars': Avraham's physical children would have bodies that shine above the stars. He returns to the two 'lech lecha's: Moriah is the source of hora'ah, where the Sanhedrin needs the greatest bodily rachmanus, so the second one is the more precious.

title.en: Noach's spark and every Jew's inheritance

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Noach found favor because Avraham's spark was within him, as sefarim explain that a person is drawn to the places and things that hold sparks he must raise, which is also the reason for galus. Every Jew was once part of Avraham and carries his spark, which, as the Chiddushei HaRim explains 'Magen Avraham', Hashem guards so that it is never lost.

title.en: Not to despair; rejoicing in the inheritance

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that the failures of Bereishis teach a person not to despair when his own fresh start after the Yamim Noraim falls apart, since the light began with 'lech lecha'. He brings the bracha said over an inheritance, explains that our body, its 248 limbs matching the gematria of Avraham, is our inheritance from Avraham, and calls to learn the parsha with joy in that inheritance.

catalogTitle: The נסיון of the עקידה: An Inspiration for our Generation

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that at the Akeidah Avraham Avinu chose to give up his love for Yitzchak with mesiras nefesh in a time of hester panim, and so charged the Jews of the last generation before Moshiach with the strength to keep their emunah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach asks what made the Akeidah the hardest test, when being thrown into the fire seems harder. He explains Avraham's complaint that his only heir was Eliezer: Eliezer was a spiritual child who would spread Hashem's name, but good midos pass only from a biological parent to a child, and Hashem promised that Yitzchak would carry them. The command 'kach na' left room to pray, as a tzaddik prays when a decree affects others. Since the deeds of the fathers are a sign for the children, the Akeidah, with its hester panim and lost madreigos, foreshadows the last test before Moshiach. Done at the beginning of place, time and soul, it charged the end of all three. Avraham had to overcome a love for Yitzchak that the words 'asher ahavta' created; he chose emunah over midos, and when Yitzchak was spared he received both. The Mashgiach ends with 'Avraham, Avraham' as Hashem's affection for Jews with mesiras nefesh today.

en: Avraham had a spiritual child in Eliezer, who passed on his Torah, but he lacked a biological child, the only way good midos are passed on.
Because the deeds of the fathers are a sign for the children, the hester panim Avraham felt at the Akeidah is the test of the last generation before Moshiach.
The Akeidah took place at the beginning of place, time and soul, and so it charged the end of place, time and soul with emunah.
The Mashgiach quotes tzaddikim that in the last days nothing in Yiddishkeit can be attained without mesiras nefesh.
Avraham chose emunah over the continuation of his midos, and when Yitzchak was spared he received both, so the Jewish people today have emunah and good midos.

candidateTopics: transmission of midos from parent to child

title.en: What test was the Akeidah? Avraham's complaint

summary.en: After opening words on the kedushah of a gathering, the Mashgiach notes that the Akeidah frames the Yamim Nora'im and asks why it was the hardest test, when being thrown into the fire seems harder. He brings Avraham's complaint that he has no child and only Eliezer, who passes on his Torah, and begins to explain that there are physical and spiritual children.

title.en: Midos pass only from parent to child

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Eliezer, Avraham's spiritual child, could spread Hashem's name, but the midos of the Avos, chesed, bushah and rachamim, pass only biologically, as the Tanya explains in chapter 2. Avraham wanted a nation that would sanctify Hashem through good midos, and Hashem promised him a child of his own body, Yitzchak.

title.en: The loophole in 'kach na'

summary.en: From Moshe Rabbeinu's 'let go of Me', the Mashgiach shows that a tzaddik accepts a decree on himself but prays when it falls on others. With the Derashos HaRan he reads 'kach na' as a request Avraham could have refused, and asks why he did not pray for Klal Yisrael's midos. He then brings the Ramban's rule that the deeds of the fathers are a sign for the children.

title.en: Hester panim on the way to the Akeidah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the setting of the Akeidah: a command that seemed to break Hashem's promise, the Satan's obstacles such as turning into a river, and Avraham losing his madreigos and seeing the place from afar, feeling Hashem distant. By the rule of the fathers' deeds, he says, the last test before Moshiach will be such a test of hester panim, and our generation is near the end.

title.en: Beginning of place, time and soul

summary.en: Avraham knew that his conduct would be duplicated by the Jews of ikvesa d'Meshicha facing the Satan's modern pritzus and apikorsus, so he had to charge them with emunah shleimah. The Mashgiach explains that the world is made of place, time and soul, which meet on Yom Kippur in the Kodesh HaKodashim, and that the Akeidah took place at the beginning of all three: Avraham, on Har HaMoriah, on Yom Kippur.

title.en: Mesiras nefesh, and the love 'asher ahavta' created

summary.en: The Mashgiach quotes the Imrei Emes and the Belzer Rav that in the last days nothing in Yiddishkeit is attained without mesiras nefesh, and that a traditional Yiddishkeit will not last. He then explains that the words 'asher ahavta' created in Avraham a love for Yitzchak above nature, and overcoming that love was the test.

title.en: Two choices: midos or emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Avraham at the Akeidah as if placed in our generation of hester panim, minus and pritzus. He had two choices: ask Hashem to release him for the sake of children with his midos, or suppress his love with mesiras nefesh and so ensure emunah for the Jews before Moshiach. He chose emunah, though it deepened his distance, and the Mashgiach shows both sides in gematrios of 'vayar es hamakom merachok'.

title.en: Granted both: Yitzchak spared

summary.en: Yitzchak was spared and the ram brought in his place, so Avraham received both: children with his midos and children with mesiras nefesh for emunah. The Mashgiach says the Jewish people today are both merciful, modest and kind and believers the children of believers, navigating with mesiras nefesh to the shores of geulah, and draws on gematrios of the year 5764.

title.en: 'Avraham, Avraham': Hashem's fondness today

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi that the double 'Avraham, Avraham' is an expression of fondness, and says Hashem says the same to Jews today who have mesiras nefesh for Torah, for emunah and for chinuch. He calls this the message of the Akeidah reading of Rosh Hashanah 5764 and closes with a tefillah for the geulah in their merit.

catalogTitle: רבינו בחיי - לך לך מארץ של רשעים

oneLiner.en: Following Rabbeinu Bachya on Lech Lecha, the Mashgiach explains that Avraham first had to leave the society of the wicked, and draws from the parsha lessons on bad company, on Avraham as the first Jew and root of Moshiach, and on how even Og's deed not for Heaven's sake served the redemption.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach introduces Rabbeinu Bachya's commentary and begins with the passuk that one who walks with the wise becomes wise. He brings the Rambam that a person is by nature drawn after his surroundings, adds the Chazon Ish's answer that today one hides in the yeshiva, and warns that even in a yeshiva one must choose one's friends. Rabbeinu Bachya reads Lech Lecha as Avraham's command to leave Nimrod's wicked society, yet the yetzer hara follows, as in the story of Reb Mendel and as Lot followed Avraham. Lech lecha also means going to one's own root. The Torah does not first describe Avraham's righteousness, because, like Amram in the Maharal, he was chosen as the first Jew for whom the world was made. The Mashgiach then treats Avraham's change of tactics in Eretz Yisrael, why Canaan held the land, Avraham's kedushas einayim, and the four kings. Og, named after the matzos, reported Lot's capture not for Heaven's sake, yet saved the sparks of Moshiach.

en: According to the Rambam, a person is created to be drawn after the views and deeds of his surroundings, so he must seek the company of the righteous and the wise and keep away from the wicked.
Rabbeinu Bachya explains that Lech Lecha commanded Avraham to leave the society of the wicked of his generation, since staying among them would take away his free choice.
Even one who leaves bad company is pursued by the yetzer hara, which makes new plans, so the struggle needs ever new strategies.
The Torah does not first describe Avraham's righteousness, because he was chosen as the first Jew, the root of Klal Yisrael for whom the world was created, and not on account of his merits.
Og, who brought Avraham the news of Lot's capture with bad intent, nevertheless caused the rescue of the families from whom Moshiach was to come, and so was named after the matzos Sarah was baking.
The Mashgiach concludes that if even Og's act not for Heaven's sake had such a share in bringing Moshiach, every small deed a Jew does for Hashem's sake is a source of the true Moshiach.

candidateTopics: the yetzer hara follows the oved Hashem

title.en: Why learn Rabbeinu Bachya

summary.en: The Mashgiach introduces Rabbeinu Bachya's commentary on the Chumash, which gathers pshat, philosophy and kabbalah, mentions the Chasam Sofer's regard for it, and explains that during these parshiyos he will share pieces of it that bring emunah, bitachon and simchah.

title.en: Walking with the wise: the Rambam on surroundings

summary.en: Rabbeinu Bachya opens the parsha with the passuk that one who walks with the wise becomes wise. The Mashgiach reads the Rambam in Hilchos Deos that a person is by nature drawn after his surroundings and must even go to the desert to escape a wicked society, tells of the Chazon Ish's answer that today one hides in the yeshiva, and says that even within a yeshiva one must choose good friends.

title.en: Lech Lecha: leaving the wicked, and the yetzer hara follows

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads Rabbeinu Bachya that Avraham had to separate from the wicked of his generation, since among them he would lose his free choice, and explains each part of Lech Lecha as leaving land, birthplace and family. He then tells how the yetzer hara met Reb Mendel in Eretz Yisrael, to show that the yetzer hara also makes plans and the battle needs new strategies.

title.en: Lot goes along; Ashrei ha'ish; going to one's root

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Lot, who went along with Avraham, is the bad side that clings to every servant of Hashem, and that separating from the wicked is the entry ticket to Tehillim, which opens with Ashrei ha'ish. He notes that the Shulchan Aruch opens with not being ashamed before scoffers, and explains lech lecha as going to oneself, one's soul and root, the first and the last of Avraham's trials.

title.en: Why the Torah doesn't say who Avraham was

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the parsha opens with Lech Lecha without telling of Avraham's righteousness. He brings the Maharal on why the Torah does not name Amram and Yocheved at first: the redemption had to come regardless of the parents' merit. Likewise Avraham was not chosen for being a tzaddik; the world needed a first Jew, the root of Klal Yisrael and of Moshiach.

title.en: Blessing and curse; Avraham's change of approach

summary.en: On 'I will bless those who bless you', the Mashgiach brings Rabbeinu Bachya and the Ramban that in Ur Kasdim Avraham was cursed and scorned. He brings the Chasam Sofer's answer why Avraham was a zealot there but acted gently in Eretz Yisrael: a zealot may act when he has nothing to lose. He then explains that Canaan held Eretz Yisrael because a servant may hold his master's land, and applies this to Yishmael.

title.en: Hinei na yadati: Avraham's holiness of the eyes

summary.en: On 'now I know that you are a beautiful woman', the Mashgiach brings Rashi and the Gemara that Iyov did not look at a maiden, while Avraham did not even look at his own wife, and says each person should learn from the Avos to guard his eyes according to his strength. He then brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on the deeper pshat and explains that Avraham saw it now as a sign that he was entering an impure place.

title.en: The four kings and Og's name

summary.en: Rabbeinu Bachya brings the Midrash that the four kings correspond to the four exiles, so Avraham's victory is a sign that Klal Yisrael will overcome them. Rashi identifies the fugitive as Og, who came intending that Avraham be killed, and the Midrash says he was named Og because Sarah was baking matzos. The Mashgiach asks what Og has to do with matzos and why Avraham risked his life for the five kings.

title.en: Sparks of Moshiach in Sedom and the power of matzah

summary.en: Through the Midrash that the war took place on the night of Pesach, the Mashgiach explains that in Sedom, through Lot's family, were sparks of Moshiach, and that matzah holds the power of all redemptions, as shown by the afikoman and the story of the Ropshitzer baking matzos during Napoleon's war. He adds that one must merit to be the cause of a kiddush Hashem, as Pharaoh did and Hitler did not.

title.en: Og's deed not for Heaven's sake, and every deed for Heaven's sake

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that Og, though acting not for Heaven's sake like Balak, caused the rescue of Lot's family and the sparks of Moshiach, and so was named for the matzos baked that night. He describes Og's great stature, which he connects to the letters of Hashem's Name, and Moshe's battle with him as a great kiddush Hashem. He concludes that every small deed done for Hashem's sake is a source of Moshiach.

catalogTitle: אשרינו כשבא פרשת לך לך' מתחיל פרשיות האבות!

oneLiner.en: Opening from Lech Lecha, where the world gains the Avos and a covenant with Hashem, the Mashgiach explains that our low generation, the 'heels' that carry all generations, is tested above all in emunah, and teaches how to fight doubts without debating them.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by contrasting the troubled parshiyos before Lech Lecha with Lech Lecha itself, where Avraham Avinu arrives, Hashem makes a covenant with him, and every Jew can renew his own bond with Hashem. He turns to the trials in emunah of our time and recalls the dispute whether emunah is itself a mitzvah or the foundation of all mitzvos. Our generation, he says, is the heel of the body: the lowest, yet it carries all the earlier generations, as the Arizal told Rav Chaim Vital. Today's tests are unprecedented, so a bochur who withstands them is very precious above. Each generation has its special test, as the Divrei Chaim's story with machine-made tzitzis shows, and ours is emunah. The Mashgiach teaches not to argue with doubts, which only entangle like a spider's web, but to push them away, to accept mesiras nefesh, to pray that the trial be shortened, never to despair, and to strengthen mind and heart through Torah and tefillah.

en: With Lech Lecha the world receives Avraham Avinu and Hashem's covenant with him, and every Jew should renew his own covenant with Hashem and rejoice in being part of the Jewish people.
Emunah is the foundation on which all the mitzvos stand.
Our generation is the lowest, the heels of the body, yet all generations stand on it and Moshiach comes to it.
Every generation is created for a particular test, and the main test of the generation before Moshiach is emunah.
Doubts in emunah should not be answered or debated but pushed out, since the yetzer hara is clever and arguing only entangles a person more.
Fighting doubts in emunah is a war against Amalek, and through Torah, tefillah and never despairing a Jew wins it.

trials of emunah in our generation

title.en: Lech Lecha and the foundation of emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the corruption of the earlier parshiyos with Lech Lecha, which brings Avraham Avinu, Eretz Yisroel, the covenants and milah, and says every Jew should make a new covenant with Hashem. He then turns to the trials in emunah and the dispute whether emunah is a mitzvah or the foundation of all mitzvos.

title.en: The lowest generation carries all the others

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares the generations to a body, with ours as the heels on which the whole body stands, and tells how the Arizal explained to Rav Chaim Vital that Hashem measures greatness by the generation. Moshiach comes specifically to the lowest generation, which will then become the greatest.

title.en: Unprecedented trials and the worth of a bochur

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how Jews in exile once lived apart from the goyim, while today they are exposed to trials no generation had, like a child thrown into the sea. A bochur who learns, davens and guards himself earns merits for all of Klal Yisroel, and the generation on which all generations stand is tested in emunah, on which all mitzvos stand.

title.en: Acquiring emunah; bad thoughts and the two souls

summary.en: The Mashgiach lists the ways to acquire emunah: guarding oneself, learning with hasmadah, davening, chesed, good middos and quick teshuvah. Bringing the Tanya on the two souls, he explains that bad thoughts come from the body, not the soul, so a person should not be shaken by them but fight them.

title.en: Each generation's test: tzitzis then, emunah now

summary.en: The Mashgiach says each generation is created for a particular thing, and tells how in the Divrei Chaim's time a factory flooded the land with machine-made tzitzis until it burned down. Today the test is emunah, through foreign ideas in books and papers, and a doubt that enters the mind must be pushed out with all one's strength rather than answered.

title.en: The spider's web: do not debate the yetzer hara

summary.en: With the parable of a fly caught in a spider's web, the Mashgiach shows that struggling with doubts only entangles a person more; the yetzer hara is clever and can bring proofs from Gemara and Chassidus. Instead one should spit at him and say that he comes from a people that gave its life for Hashem, from Avraham Avinu and from the martyrs of France, as Avraham answered the Satan at the Akeidah.

title.en: A private geulah from the trial

summary.en: The Mashgiach says trials of emunah can last weeks, months or years, each measured out in Heaven, and afterwards a person sees clear emunah like a sky without clouds. Like the geulah of Klal Yisroel, which has a fixed time but can come sooner through merit, each Jew's private geulah can be hastened by prayer and by accepting mesiras nefesh, as at Krias Shema.

title.en: Bechirah, Klal Yisroel and the war against Amalek

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a person has bechirah so that he can choose and earn reward, and that one should bind himself to Klal Yisroel, the tzaddikim and the Avos, knowing the doubts are a spirit of folly. Fighting them is the war against Amalek, whose name equals 'safek' (doubt); Amalek came after 'is Hashem among us', and the serpent seduced Chava in emunah.

title.en: Never despair; Torah, tefillah and the battlefield

summary.en: The Mashgiach says doubts may come from a decree, which pushing them away annuls; one must never despair but start again from the beginning, for Hashem helps. Hashem sends Jewish bochurim into this war like soldiers, the spark of love for Hashem cannot be extinguished, and every victory earns a medal; the main weapons are learning with hasmadah, which cleanses the mind, and tefillah, which strengthens the heart.

catalogTitle: ביאור על מחלוקת אברם עם לוט; גנות עמי הארץ שמחרחרי ריב בין הצדיקים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains the quarrel between Avraham's and Lot's shepherds through the story of Bar Kamtza: a small dispute among great people becomes a destructive machlokes when the ignorant turn it into politics.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the pasuk that there was a 'riv' between the shepherds of Avraham and Lot, while Avraham asks that there be no 'merivah', and asks what each word means. He turns to the Gemara's story of Kamtza and Bar Kamtza and asks why the Chachamim heeded Rabbi Zechariah ben Avkulas. He explains Rabbi Zechariah's fear of spreading a false halachah, bringing the Yam Shel Shlomo, and shows that the dispute was only over assessing the situation. Citing a letter of the Chasam Sofer, he decries machlokes that ignorant people drag into politics, unlike healthy disputes between talmidei chachamim. The Chachamim yielded to avoid a political split. So too, Lot's shepherds wanted to join the warring sides, turning a small 'merivah' into a 'riv'. Finally, from the Chasam Sofer and a Midrash on Tidal, he contrasts Avraham's tactics and warns that today's galus bites with a kiss.

en: A 'merivah' (feminine form) is a small, weak dispute, as between Avraham and Lot; a 'riv' (masculine) is a strong quarrel, as among the shepherds who tied it to the war over the land.

Rabbi Zechariah ben Avkulas refused to offer the Caesar's blemished sacrifice even for pikuach nefesh because people would conclude that blemished animals may be offered, and one must give one's life rather than falsify a halachah.
A machlokes between talmidei chachamim over halachah is healthy and l'shem shamayim, but a machlokes with political undercurrents, discussed by everyone in the street, is destructive.
The Chachamim yielded to Rabbi Zechariah because the question had been taken up by political factions, the peace party and the war party, and a split in Klal Yisrael was worse than the sin itself.

Lot's shepherds wanted to join one side of the war between the Canaanites and Perizzites and the descendants of Shem, so as to gain the land, and Avraham separated from Lot to keep their small dispute from growing.

Following the Midrash on Tidal and Esav's kiss, the Mashgiach says that the galus of Edom, which once tried to bite the Jews, now bites with a kiss, by drawing them close, and he says Jews must not be drawn into its culture.

candidateTopics: the four kings and the four kingdoms

title.en: Riv and merivah; the story of Bar Kamtza

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the pesukim about the quarrel between the shepherds of Avraham and Lot and asks what 'riv' and 'merivah' mean. He then tells the Gemara's story of Kamtza and Bar Kamtza and asks why the Chachamim had to heed Rabbi Zechariah ben Avkulas.

title.en: Why Rabbi Zechariah would not allow the offering

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a Roman ruler would never accept a tiny blemish as a reason, so the Chachamim saw it as pikuach nefesh. He brings the Gemara in Bava Kamma and the Yam Shel Shlomo that one must give one's life rather than falsify a halachah, and explains that Rabbi Zechariah feared a false halachah would spread; the Chachamim disagreed only in assessing that danger.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's letter: two kinds of machlokes

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a letter of the Chasam Sofer that a machlokes in an earlier generation, with disgrace of talmidei chachamim, held back Moshiach, and that true bnei Torah should stay silent and learn. He distinguishes a healthy machlokes in halachah from one with political undercurrents that everyone discusses, and explains that great poskim rule from daas Torah, which outsiders cannot judge.

title.en: Peace party and war party at the Churban

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that at the time of the Churban there were two factions: the Chachamim under Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai, who wanted peace with Rome, and the biryonim under Abba Sikra, who wanted war. The question of the Caesar's offering became a political platform, so the Chachamim stayed passive and followed Rabbi Zechariah to avoid a split in Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Lot's shepherds and the war over the land

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies this to Avraham and Lot: Lot's shepherds wanted to join the winning side in the war between the Canaanites and Perizzites and the descendants of Shem. He explains that 'merivah' is feminine and weak, a small dispute over whether the promise of the land already took effect, while 'riv' is masculine, the shepherds' political quarrel, and so Avraham asked Lot to separate.

title.en: Why Avraham stopped fighting in Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer: in Ur Kasdim Avraham was a zealous fighter who broke the idols and was thrown into the fire, but in Eretz Yisrael he lived in peace with his neighbors. Alone in Ur, he could not raise students and gave his life; with 'Lech lecha' he was promised a great following, so he was no longer permitted to risk his life.

title.en: The vav of Tidal and Esav's kiss

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash that the vav in 'v'Sidal' among the four kings is part of the name. He connects it to Rashi on Esav's kiss: Esav wanted to bite Yaakov and, unable, kissed him. He then introduces the galus of Edom, the Roman Church that ruled Europe, the fourth of the four galuyos named in the zemiros and Maoz Tzur, which the Midrash links to the four kings.

title.en: Edom bites with a kiss

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Edom first bit the Jews with persecutions, the Crusades and the Inquisition, and when that failed it now bites with a kiss: friendship, interfaith meetings and assimilation. Tidal, 'king of nations', is the fourth kingdom of many peoples under one church, and the vav of joining is its way of tormenting Jews, so he says Jews must not fall into its web or take on its culture.

catalogTitle: A פרשה of .פקידת עקרות The מסירת נפש of אברהם אבינו for the מצוה of הכנסת אורחים and his Reward

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach shows that Parshas Vayera is a time of pekidas akaros, and that Avraham Avinu's self-sacrifice for his guests is why Adam and Chava had to let Sarah into the Me'aras HaMachpelah despite their discomfort.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the idea that a Jew who keeps Shabbos becomes a partner in creation, and that this week's sedra carries the Torah readings of both days of Rosh Hashanah, making it a time of pekidas akaros, remembering the barren. He widens barrenness to Torah learning that produces no chiddushim and tefillah without heart, lists the seven barren women, and adds Tziyon as the barren mother. He then turns to Avraham Avinu's hachnasas orchim three days after his milah, Rashi on the calf he prepared, and a midrash in the Yalkut Reuveni: the calf was the angel Refael, who led Avraham into the Me'aras HaMachpelah, and Avraham then made a calf through Sefer Yetzirah. After a discussion of such creations and of milk and meat, the Mashgiach asks why the cave was revealed 38 years early, and answers that Avraham's disregard of his own discomfort obligated Adam and Chava to disregard theirs when Sarah was buried.

en: A Jew who keeps Shabbos becomes Hashem's partner, since each Shabbos creates the world anew for the next six days.
Because Parshas Vayera holds the Torah readings of both days of Rosh Hashanah, this Shabbos is a time of pekidas akaros.
Barrenness also describes Torah learning that yields no chiddushim and davening without heart, and on this Shabbos one can daven not to be barren in Torah and tefillah.
According to the midrash, the calf Avraham chased was the angel Refael, who led him into the Me'aras HaMachpelah.
Avraham's self-sacrifice for his guests, ignoring his own pain, is what obligated Adam and Chava to ignore their discomfort and admit Sarah into the cave.

title.en: Shabbos, partnership in creation, and Rosh Hashanah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem created the world for six days and each Shabbos renews it, so one who says Vayechulu becomes a partner in creation. He notes that this week's sedra holds the Torah readings of both days of Rosh Hashanah, making it a time of pekidas akaros, and brings the passuk that there will be no barren among Yidden.

title.en: Barrenness in Torah and tefillah; the seven akaros

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a man with many children can still be barren if his Torah bears no fruit, and likewise davening without heart. He lists the seven barren women, adds Tziyon as the barren mother awaiting her children, and says this Shabbos is a time to daven for barren relatives, for one's own Torah and tefillah, and for Tziyon.

title.en: Avraham's self-sacrifice for his guests

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Avraham Avinu at 99, three days after his milah, sitting in the heat waiting for guests and slaughtering three calves to serve them tongue with mustard. He reads the passuk of the calf 'asher asah' and brings Rashi that it means he prepared it, and that he served each dish as it was ready.

title.en: The calf that was the angel Refael

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the midrash in the Yalkut Reuveni: the calf Avraham chased was the angel Refael, who ran into the Me'aras HaMachpelah, where Avraham saw Adam and Chava and the light of Gan Eden. Having lost time, Avraham created a calf with Sefer Yetzirah, and the Mashgiach explains what Sefer Yetzirah is, citing the Gemara's calf made for Shabbos and the Maharal's golem.

title.en: Is a Sefer Yetzirah creation a person or meat?

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings an Acharon who asks whether a golem can count for a minyan and proves it cannot from the Gemara about Rabbi Eliezer freeing a slave to complete a minyan. He then asks whether a calf made with Sefer Yetzirah may be cooked in butter and says it may, since it is not meat descended from the first animals, and contrasts this with a clone.

title.en: Milk and meat at Avraham's meal

summary.en: The Mashgiach offers a new reading: Avraham served milk and meat together because the calf 'asher asah' was made with Sefer Yetzirah. Rashi, who learns pshat where possible, explains instead that the milk came first, and that no bread was served because Sarah became tamei, so it was not one meal.

title.en: Why reveal the cave 38 years early? Chava's protest

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the angel interrupted Avraham's mitzvah to reveal the Me'aras HaMachpelah a year before Yitzchak's birth, 38 years before Sarah's burial. He brings a midrash that when Avraham came to bury Sarah, Adam and Chava walked out in protest because Sarah's righteousness shamed them; Adam relented, but Avraham had to plead with Chava and bring her back, which explains 'v'acharei chen'.

title.en: Measure for measure: Avraham's reward

summary.en: The Mashgiach argues that Chava was in the right, comparing her claim to the din of neighbors sharing a fence for privacy in the Rambam. He answers that since Avraham ignored his own discomfort for his guests, measure for measure Adam and Chava had to ignore theirs, and so Hashem revealed the cave at that very moment, to show that the claim was already answered.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the avos are the heart of the Jewish people, as Yerushalayim is the heart of the world and tefillah the service of the heart, and that a Jew, as Avraham's child, is good in his essence.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with tefillah: its essence is emunah, it is the 'service of the heart', and the one blessing that requires kavanah is the blessing of the avos, because our emunah comes from them. To explain how Chazal knew that service of the heart means tefillah, he shows that man is a small world: each part of the world matches a limb, and Yerushalayim, the place of prayer for all nations, is the world's heart. So too the blessing of the avos is the heart of the Jewish people, and the parshiyos of the avos must be learned by living with them. He then takes up the Ramban's charge that Avraham sinned by going down to Egypt, and asks why the Torah never says why Avraham was chosen. His answer: there had to be a Jewish people, and a Jew is a tzaddik in essence, his sins only incidental. He closes that learning Torah carries us back into the time of the avos.

en: Tefillah is the 'service of the heart', and its essence is emunah; the blessing of the avos, the source of our emunah, is the one blessing that requires kavanah.
Man is a small world, and Yerushalayim, the house of prayer, is the heart of the world; therefore the service of the heart is tefillah.
The avos are the heart of the Jewish people, and their parshiyos must be learned by living with them, as an example for oneself.
The Torah does not state Avraham's merits, just as it first hides the names of Moshe's parents, because the Jewish people had to come into being regardless.
Every Jew is a tzaddik in essence; his sins are only incidental, which is why korbanos and teshuvah help a Jew.
Learning Torah is not reading history: it carries a Jew back into the time he is learning about, so that he lives with the avos.

title.en: Tefillah, emunah and the blessing of the avos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that tefillah means believing that whatever one needs comes from Hashem, and that it is the 'service of the heart', not lip service. Of all the blessings, only the blessing of the avos requires kavanah, because all our emunah comes from the avos, as the parsha says of Avraham that he believed in Hashem.

title.en: Man as a small world

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how Chazal knew that 'with all your heart' means tefillah. He explains that the world is built on a pattern, like a fern whose every leaf is a small fern, and that man, made with 'na'aseh adam' and in the image of G-d, contains the whole world; each part of the world corresponds to a limb.

title.en: Yerushalayim, the heart of the world

summary.en: Bringing the Kuzari, the Mashgiach explains that Yerushalayim is the heart of the world: the whole world revolves around it, and it is the house of prayer for all nations, where people of every kind come to daven at the Kosel. Since a person's heart corresponds to Yerushalayim, Chazal understood that the service of the heart is tefillah.

title.en: Living with the avos when learning the parsha

summary.en: The blessing of the avos is the heart of the Jewish people, from which it comes and to which it returns. Therefore, the Mashgiach says, it is not enough to say the words of the parshiyos of Bereishis; one must contemplate how the avos lived and served Hashem, learn them with commentaries like a Tosfos, and put oneself into their place.

title.en: The Ramban: Avraham sinned

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ramban that Avraham committed a great sin by going down to Egypt in the famine and by exposing Sarah to danger, and was punished with the exile of his children in Egypt. This is surprising, since Rabbeinu Yonah teaches that a tzaddik must be judged favorably even without a visible merit, and the Torah itself praises Avraham as Hashem's beloved who listened to His voice.

title.en: Why the Torah hides Avraham's merits

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Torah calls Noach a tzaddik but tells nothing of Avraham's righteousness or his ordeal in Ur Kasdim before he is chosen with great blessings. He answers with the Maharal on parshas Shemos: Moshe's parents first appear unnamed, because the Jewish people's redemption is the purpose of creation and had to happen.

title.en: There had to be a redeemer and a nation

summary.en: Amram and Yocheved were great tzaddikim and merited Moshe, but had they not been, the redeemer would have come anyway, just as Moshiach will come at the final appointed time even without teshuvah. Only later does the Torah name the parents. In the same way the Torah omits Avraham's righteousness and mesirus nefesh, because the Jewish people had to be.

title.en: Every Jew is a tzaddik in essence

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains, following the Maharal, that every Jew holds an inner point from Avraham that never sins, as the Rambam shows from coercing a person until he says 'I want'. A Jew's sin is incidental and can be washed off like dirt, which is why korbanos and teshuvah help him; this answers Avraham's question 'how will I know' with the korbanos.

title.en: The Ramban's charge as praise

summary.en: Because Avraham is good in essence, the Torah does not list his good deeds; Hashem simply chose him. The Mashgiach explains that the Ramban's pointing out a sin at the very start of Avraham's story is a great compliment: even with a sin he was chosen, since in a Jew a sin is only incidental. In the end of days the beauty of every Jew will be revealed and all sins forgotten.

title.en: Torah carries us back to the avos

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to learning the parsha like a Tosfos and living with the avos. He brings the Midrash that Rebbi cursed Nebuchadnezzar when reading the Megillah but not when learning Yirmiyahu, since in Yirmiyahu's time he was still a king; Torah is alive and carries the learner into its time. So too, every Jew is part of Avraham and must live with the avos when learning their parshiyos.

catalogTitle: "וישמע אברם כי נשבה אחיו" - נשבה ניצוץ משיח

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that after the failed worlds of Adam and Noach, the world's tikkun had to come through Avraham and the Jewish people no matter what, which is why the Torah gives Avraham no introduction and why the kings captured Lot, from whom Moshiach was to come.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by calling Bereishis and Noach a world that did not succeed: Adam sinned, the generation of the flood corrupted even the animals and the earth, and the new start after the flood was spoiled by those who sinned in the ark. Since creation was handed to man, each person's share of it rises or falls with his deeds; Noach's share, and Eretz Yisrael, stayed pure. Lech Lecha begins the world of tikkun through Avraham and his descendants. The Mashgiach brings the Ramban's charge that Avraham sinned by going to Egypt, and the Zohar's defense through Sarah's merit. He then shows that the Torah hides the merits of Moshe's parents and of Avraham because the Jewish people and the final redemption must come regardless. The kings captured Lot because Moshiach was to descend from him. He closes with Esav, who bites with a kiss, and warns against today's mingling with the nations.

en: Bereishis and Noach describe two attempts at a proper world that did not succeed; Lech Lecha begins the world of tikkun through Avraham.
Hashem gave creation into man's hands, so each person's share of the world flourishes or is spoiled according to his deeds; the sins of the flood generation spoiled even the animals and the earth.
The Torah does not say who Moshe's parents were at his birth, nor what merits made Avraham chosen, because the Jewish people had to come into being regardless of anyone's merits.
Following the Ramban at the end of Haazinu, the Mashgiach says the redemption will come at its set time whether or not the Jews do teshuvah, and likewise every Jew must in the end reach his tikkun.
The four kings captured Lot because they knew that Moshiach was to come from him, and Avraham went to war to make sure Moshiach would come.
The exile of Edom first bit the Jews openly and now bites them with a kiss, through friendship and mingling, which the Mashgiach calls a great danger.
