title.en: Avraham seeks a match for Yitzchak first

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Avraham sought a match for Yitzchak before remarrying himself, and brings Rabbi Yonasan's answer from Rashi's 'bakol', that Avraham already had a son and daughter. He then brings the Zohar that Avraham shares the root of Hillel in chesed and Yitzchak that of Shammai in din.

title.en: Each soul receives Torah through its root

summary.en: With a mashal of water poured into a white or red glass, the Mashgiach explains that the Torah takes on the color of the soul that receives it, and applies this to Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel on peru urevu and to Avraham and Yitzchak. He adds that the world was first planned with din and joined with rachamim, and that in the future the halacha will follow Beis Shammai.

title.en: What chesed and din are

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Beis Shammai's view of two males from the original plan of din, and defines chesed as outward, straight light, the right side, and din as contraction inward, the left side. He shows that the avodah is to make the right prevail, from the order of putting on shoes and the longer right strap, and from the dispute whether the world was created in Nisan or Tishrei.

title.en: Yishmael and Esav: the kelipos of chesed and din

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that in kelipah, too, there are chesed and din: Yishmael is the kelipah of chesed, fallen love, and Esav the kelipah of din, murder. Each nation follows its heavenly sar, which he shows from their days of rest and calendars: Yishmael by the moon alone, Esav by the sun, and the Jews by the moon while reckoning the sun as well, because only they join the two.

title.en: Why Yishmael held Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar that Bnei Yishmael were given rule over Eretz Yisrael for their milah, and asks what share they have in it. Using the Rambam's reason that milah weakens desire and the Gemara that Arabia took nine measures of zenus, he concludes that their milah is no milah at all, so the holiness of a Jew is essential, and Eretz Yisrael, given for the bris, was entrusted to them so no one could mistake it as theirs.

title.en: Fire, the bris and Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the four elements, with fire, energy, as the spiritual root of all, matched by the Torah and milah, both called a bris of fire, and by Eretz Yisrael, the foundation of creation, as Rashi on the first passuk teaches. Since the land of fire was taken from the Arabs, they were given oil as a cheap substitute. He returns to the Jews' pairing of chesed with din, shown in teruah never standing without tekiah and Yitzchak never standing alone.

title.en: Right over left in writing and in the home

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that no sidra has Yitzchak without Avraham or Yaakov, and that a Jew writes from right to left to put chesed first, while each letter is drawn from the left to join din to it. He applies the same to the man going before the woman, contrasting the order of Yaakov's and Esav's households in Vayishlach and the gentile custom, and stresses that the Torah governs even such small things.

title.en: Not from the daughters of Canaan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Avraham's charge not to take a wife from the Canaanites through the Bnei Yissaschar, citing the Rebbe of Lublin, that the seven nations are seven bad middos, and the Ohr HaChaim that in kelipah the female is stronger, so Canaan is the nation that submits chesed to din. Following the Yitav Lev, he reads Eliezer's worry and Rivkah's answer 'I will go' as the question who leads in the home.

title.en: Why the angel of Sedom came to Avraham

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the angel sent to overturn Sedom first came to Avraham, and gives three answers: a malach of din may not go without malachim of rachamim; the angel needed Avraham's psak whether a Moabite woman may marry in, since Dovid must come from Lot; and Avraham's escorting gave the angel his strength of chesed. He supports the last from Pharaoh escorting the Jews and from Rivkah being barren despite her family's blessing.

title.en: The shaliach and the clay pots

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chiddushei HaRim that Moshe's spies failed because they kept some self-will instead of fully nullifying themselves to their sender, and that every Jew is a shaliach of Hashem who succeeds through such bittul. Yehoshua's spies carried clay pots to remember that, like a kli cheres whose worth is only in its use, they had no worth of their own beyond their mission.

title.en: Sarah's death in mesiras nefesh

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings from the sefarim and the Chasam Sofer that Sarah died not from fright but from a longing of mesiras nefesh when she heard of the Akeidah, and that only her body's elements passed while she herself remained bound to the root of Eretz Yisrael. Avraham, envious of her level, called himself a stranger, and the Bnei Ches answered that he is a prince of G-d who must stay to teach the world.

title.en: Sarah's 127 years and the years of youth

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Rabbi Akiva woke his sleeping listeners by asking why Esther ruled 127 provinces, and explains with the Chasam Sofer that Sarah rose at night to make up the years of infancy when she could not serve Hashem. From here he speaks of the great power of the years of youth and the danger of sleeping them away, like Choni HaMe'agel's seventy years.

title.en: Uprooting Yishmael, starting within

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the years of youth belong to chesed and love, as Shlomo wrote Shir HaShirim in his youth, and must be harnessed for holiness rather than the kelipah of chesed. Since the parsha lists the generations of Yishmael, it holds the power to rectify them; each person must find and uproot the Yishmael within himself, and through this the world will be freed of Yishmael.

catalogTitle: צד א: נצחיות של זיווגי ישראל' וחילוק בין הר המוריה וחברון.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Har HaMoriah, the place of revealed Shechinah that could be destroyed, with the Me'aras HaMachpelah in Chevron, the hidden place of the avos and their couples that no churban can touch, and applies it to the eternity of a Jewish marriage and to a new beis medrash.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Shlomo HaMelech's dedication of the Beis HaMikdash: Shlomo foresaw a time of hester panim without a Mikdash, yet the Shechinah would remain among Jews in a mikdash me'at. Turning to Chayei Sarah, he asks why the Torah would name holy Chevron, Kiryas Arba, after the giants, as in Rashi's first explanation. He explains that the Mikdash on Moriah is revelation, the place of prayer, while the Machpelah is its hidden extension, where the avos lie concealed and are present in every Jew. Churban could strike only the place of revelation; the Machpelah, a hiding within a hiding, cannot be destroyed. Moriah is fire, bought from Aravna; Machpelah is earth, bought from Efron, which never passes away. Its name, couples, shows that the bond of a true zivug, of body and soul, outlasts death. He ends by tying this to the new chevra's beis medrash, the prayers of Dovid and Shlomo, and a story from Yerushalayim.

en: Shlomo HaMelech foresaw that the Mikdash would give way to a time of hester panim, yet the Shechinah would remain among the Jews in a mikdash me'at.
Har HaMoriah and the Me'aras HaMachpelah are two aspects of one Mikdash: Moriah is revelation, the Machpelah is concealment.
Churban could strike only the Mikdash in Yerushalayim; the hidden strength of the avos in the Machpelah, present in every Jew, can never be destroyed.
The Machpelah is named for the couples buried there to show that a true zivug, of body and of soul, is not broken even by death.
Both of Rashi's explanations of the name Kiryas Arba are needed: the giants on the surface and the avos hidden below show what the Machpelah is.

A beis medrash is a mikdash me'at, holding a stone of the Mikdash, and the Mashgiach wishes that the new chevra be a place of learning, davening and ahavas chaverim, bound to the avos and the tzaddikim.

title.en: Shlomo's foresight and the name Kiryas Arba

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how Shlomo HaMelech, at the dedication of the Mikdash, foresaw a time of hester panim when the Shechinah would remain in a mikdash me'at. He then brings Rashi's two explanations of the name Kiryas Arba and asks why the Torah would name holy Chevron after the giants.

title.en: Rachel, Leah and the power of the Machpelah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Rachel is the revealed world and Leah the hidden one, which is why Leah is buried in the Machpelah and Rachel on the road. He brings Rashi on Yosef being sent from the 'depth of Chevron' and the Gemara about Eliyahu waking the avos one by one, to show that the success of the Jews comes from the Machpelah.

title.en: Moriah is revelation, the Machpelah is hidden

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how prayers can rise both through Yerushalayim and through the Machpelah, and answers that the Machpelah is an extension of the Mikdash with a different character. Moriah, the mountain Avraham chose for prayer, is revelation; the Machpelah, a cave under a cave, is the hidden presence of the avos in every Jew, so one does not turn toward it in davening.

title.en: Churban cannot reach the Machpelah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that churban, being cut off from revelation, could come only to the Mikdash, never to the Machpelah, and that is why they had to be two places; Chevron means connection. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'hester within hester' and compares Yerushalayim to the element of fire, which can go out, and the Machpelah to earth, which never passes away.

title.en: Aravna and Efron; the spies and the giants

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that both the Mikdash and the Machpelah were bought for full money: Dovid bought from Aravna, whose other name Ornan equals 'fire', and Avraham from Efron, whose name recalls 'earth'. The spies saw only the giants on the surface of Chevron, while Calev went down to the avos; so both of Rashi's explanations are needed to understand the Machpelah.

title.en: The eternal zivug of the Machpelah

summary.en: The Mashgiach distinguishes the zivug of the body from the eternal zivug of the soul, decreed before birth, and explains that the Machpelah is named for its couples to show that their bond lasts even in the grave, unlike the Mikdash whose bond was interrupted. He ties this to Avraham's effort to buy the cave for Sarah, to Adam and Chava, and to kiddushin learned from the field of Efron.

title.en: Why Rachel is not in the Machpelah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Rachel, who is revelation, would have brought light into the place of concealment and there could have been no galus, which is why Yaakov saw she could not be buried there. Yosef went into galus from Chevron, the place of hidden closeness, and the decree of galus was said there. He contrasts the end of Vayeira, revelation at the Akeidah, with Chayei Sarah, and brings the stones of the Mikdash scattered into every beis medrash.

title.en: The new chevra and the prayers of Dovid and Shlomo

summary.en: Turning to the newly founded chevra, the Mashgiach connects it to Dovid HaMelech, who prepared for the Mikdash, and to Shlomo who built it. He goes through Dovid's prayer that the desire to serve Hashem remain fresh forever and Shlomo's prayer at the dedication, and says the beis medrash was made so that one can reach the point in the heart where the avos are hidden.

title.en: A request in Yerushalayim, and blessings

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a time of disputes in Yerushalayim, when a visitor asked the chassidim that their place be only for learning, davening and ahavas chaverim, and the words lit a fire. He wishes the same for the new chevra, a place of connection like the couples of the Machpelah, and closes with blessings for the ingathering to Yerushalayim.

catalogTitle: שידוכים: Made in Heaven, A Reunion of נשמות , Related to שבת

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that a shidduch is made in Heaven as the reunion of one soul split in two, why kiddushin is learned from the purchase of the Me'aras HaMachpela, why the shadchan is paid, and how a shidduch is bound up with Shabbos.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Eliezer, the father of all shadchanim, whose name is never mentioned in the parsha, to show that Hashem, not the shadchan, makes every shidduch. He then asks why kiddushin with money is learned from Avraham's purchase of a burial cave, which seems a poor omen, and answers that the Me'aras HaMachpela, where couples lie together, teaches that marriage is a reunion of one soul that existed before life and continues after it. He tells the Midrash of Cleopatra's failed matchmaking and asks why a shadchan is paid at all. The malach who announces each shidduch does not truly know, so rejected proposals are steps toward the real one, as hinted in the tenth maamar, 'it is not good... a helper opposite him.' Quoting the Tzemach Tzedek, he explains the shadchan is paid for the lie that silences the Satan. Finally he links the shidduch to Shabbos and Malchus, and urges kedushah.

en: Every shidduch is decreed by Hashem before the couple is born; the shadchan does not make it, which is why Eliezer's name is not mentioned in the parsha.
Marriage is not a union but a reunion: each couple is one soul that Hashem splits into male and female and later brings back together.
Learning kiddushin from the Me'aras HaMachpela shows that the bond of the souls exists before life and continues after it, even though halachically kiddushin ends at death.
The malach who announces a shidduch does not truly know it, so a person passes through proposals that are rejected before reaching the right one.
Because a shidduch comes from so high a place the Satan prosecutes against it, and the shadchan is paid for the lie that is thrown to him, except by great tzaddikim against whom he has no hold.
A shidduch belongs to Shabbos and to Malchus, the tenth: the tenth maamar, about Chava, was really meant for Shabbos, and the kallah is like Shabbos.

title.en: Eliezer's name and the Heavenly shidduch

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Eliezer, the father of shadchanim, is never named in the parsha of the shidduch, to show that Hashem makes every match. He brings the Midrash that couples are destined together before birth, and that the parsha of shidduchim is introduced by the Me'aras HaMachpela, 'doubled' with couples.

title.en: Good simanim and kiddushin from a burial cave

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how Jews seek good omens for a chuppah, such as marrying while the moon is waxing, since the chuppah is the Rosh Hashanah of married life. He asks why kiddushin with money, kesef that speaks of longing, is learned from Avraham's purchase of a burial cave, which seems a poor omen.

title.en: Marriage as a reunion of souls

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that the Me'aras HaMachpela is the best omen: halachically kiddushin ends at death, but the bond of the souls existed before life and remains after it. Like Adam and Chava, who were one body, each couple is one soul split in two, so marriage is a reunion, and kiddushin learned from the cave shows it is an everlasting bond.

title.en: Cleopatra's matches and why pay a shadchan

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the Midrash of Cleopatra, who mocked that she too could make matches, paired her slaves overnight and found them beaten the next morning. He then asks why the Shulchan Aruch has laws of shadchanus and why one must pay the shadchan if Hashem makes the match, bringing Rabbi Yaakov Emden's saying about the shadchan.

title.en: The malach who does not know the shidduch

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the malach who announces a shidduch forty days before formation does not truly know it, as Shmuel HaNavi did not know which son of Yishai was to be king. So the malach guesses and Hashem rejects until the right one, which is why a tzaddik gave a token payment for every proposal, and he tells of a man who tried to exploit this.

title.en: The tenth maamar: 'it is not good'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara and the Zohar on counting the ten maamaros; according to the Zohar the tenth is 'it is not good for man to be alone, I will make him a helper opposite him', which corresponds to the tenth commandment, not to covet. He explains that this maamar begins with 'not good' and ends with the true match, just as shidduchim pass through rejected options.

title.en: The Satan's accusation and the shadchan's lie

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that whenever something lofty comes down the Satan prosecutes and must be thrown something, as with the broken luchos, the glass broken at a chuppah and the goat to Azazel. He brings the Tzemach Tzedek that no shidduch goes through without a lie, so the shadchan is paid for the lie; but by great tzaddikim the Satan cannot prosecute, and Eliezer thanked Hashem that he needed no lie.

title.en: The tenth maamar and Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks when the tenth maamar took place and brings Rashi that what belonged to Shabbos was done on Erev Shabbos, so a shidduch is really a matter of Shabbos, as Chassidim shout 'Shabbos' at a chasunah. He explains that the last three makkos were heavenly and that the seventh day is really the tenth, since Torah and teshuvah preceded creation.

title.en: Kallah, Shabbos and Malchus; guarding the shidduch

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Shabbos is Malchus and the kallah is Shabbos, so every chuppah is a Shabbos matter with great kedushah; menuchah, the kallah, was created on Shabbos, and the last maamar carries Hashem's name of chesed. He closes that a person can lose his shidduch by not conducting himself in kedushah, and blesses that the right shidduch come to fruition.
